items.title: Pulmonary Ionocytes Regulate CFTR-Mediated Chloride Transport in Human iPSC-Derived Epithelium.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Pulmonary ionocytes, representing approximately 1% of airway epithelial cells, exhibit high CFTR expression and unique transcriptional markers, including FOXI1, ASCL3, and V-ATPase. Their exact role in human airway physiology is incompletely understood. This study employs induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived airway epithelial models (iPSC-airways) to elucidate the role of FOXI1 in pulmonary ionocyte differentiation and function. CRISPR-Cas9 was used to generate FOXI1-knockout iPSCs, into which a doxycycline-inducible FOXI1-overexpression cassette was introduced. Edited and control lines were differentiated into airway epithelia to evaluate ionocyte formation, epithelial composition, and ion transport. Rescue studies assessed the effects of FOXI1 re-expression in a FOXI1-KO background, and the addition of inducible WT-CFTR ionocytes to F508del/F508del cystic fibrosis (CF) cultures on restoring chloride transport. FOXI1 deletion abolishes ionocyte formation and alters airway epithelial composition, with increased mucus-secreting goblet cells and decreased ciliated cells. Functional assays confirmed ionocytes as key regulators of chloride homeostasis, with FOXI1-deficient airways displaying diminished ion transport. Induction of FOXI1-overexpression restored CFTR-mediated chloride transport. Introduction of WT ionocytes into CF airway models rescued chloride transport deficits, with no rescue observed in vehicle-treated controls lacking ionocyte induction. These findings highlight FOXI1's essential role in pulmonary ionocyte development, airway cell composition, and airway chloride transport. We present a fully manipulable, gene-edited iPSC-derived system that enables investigation of ionocyte biology and function within a human airway context, highlighting them as promising therapeutic targets for respiratory disorders.

items.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.
items.abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

items.title: Targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventilator-associated pneumonia with a non-antibiotic and biofilm-disrupting live biotherapeutic: preclinical safety and efficacy study.
items.abstract: The endotracheal tube (ETT) compromises the host's bronchial defences and facilitates the formation of microbial biofilms and Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). Although antibiotics remain the cornerstone treatment, their efficacy is often compromised by poor biofilm penetration and the prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria. This reveals the need to develop novel non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. We previously engineered a non-pathogenic strain of the pulmonary bacteria Mycoplasma pneumoniae (CV2) to express anti-biofilm and bactericidal enzymes (VAP platform). We evaluated the safety of an improved version of CV2 (CV8, Mycochassis) in a miniature pig model, and its efficacy with the VAP platform (CV8_VAP) in a piglet model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced VAP. CV8_VAP was administered via intralobe instillation or nebulisation. We assessed the platform's ability to degrade biofilms formed on ETTs in vivo and its impact on the airway microbiota. We evaluated bacterial load in the lungs, inflammatory responses, histopathological and clinical outcomes. Statistics included t-tests, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U and mixed-effects rank-based methods. VAP platform reduced ETT biofilm thickness and P. aeruginosa load in lungs, with the nebulised route showing enhanced efficacy. Shannon diversity remained statistically comparable across groups in both ETTs and lung tissue. Inflammatory markers in the lung were markedly decreased, suggesting a local immunomodulatory effect. One animal receiving nebulised CV8_VAP died from a suspected anaphylactic-like reaction; no other serious adverse events were attributable to treatment. These findings suggest CV8_VAP as a promising, non-antibiotic therapeutic strategy for treating VAP caused by P. aeruginosa. items.title: Pragmatic Clinical indicators of Tuberculosis Transmission Risk: a Household Contact Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

items.title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis of lung function identifies candidate causal variants and improves polygenic prediction.
items.abstract: Most genome-wide association studies (GWASs) and polygenic score (PGS) models for lung function are based on European-ancestry individuals. Here, we performed GWASs in 17,738 Chinese individuals from the Dongfeng-Tongji (DFTJ) and Wuhan-Zhuhai (WHZH) cohorts, followed by meta-analysis with lung function GWASs from the China Kadoorie Biobank (sample size, n = 100,285), the Taiwan Biobank (n = 62,901), and European-ancestry studies (n = 400,102). Multi-ancestry fine-mapping pinpoints four novel candidate causal variants: one insertion (rs56381615, LINC02270) and three SNPs (rs6941411, PTK7; rs13315867, EPHA3; and rs2713769, ABI3BP). Cross-ancestry genetic correlations are high (0.682-0.811) but significantly lower than 1 (p < 0.005). Transcriptome-wide association analysis across 16 tissues identifies 1,374 genes, including PTK7, CUL7, and EPHA3 as leading novel candidates. Finally, we develop multi-ancestry PGS models that outperform existing models. Overall, this study quantifies cross-ancestry genetic correlation, prioritizes candidate genes, and enhances PGS prediction accuracy of lung function traits in East Asian populations.

items.title: Targeting Kynurenine Synthesis Attenuated Cigarette Smoke-Induced COPD-Like Lung Injury Driven by TALDO1-Mediated Metabolic Reprogramming.
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a devastating condition characterized by airflow limitation, inflammation, and structural lung damage. Metabolic dysregulation is recognized as a critical feature, but the key metabolic drivers remain unclear. This study identifies transaldolase1 (TALDO1) as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator in cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD pathogenesis. TALDO1 is markedly upregulated in airway epithelial cells by CS exposure. Elevated TALDO1 promotes mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas its genetic knockdown attenuates CS-induced lung function decline and pulmonary inflammation. Mechanistically, TALDO1 activation redirects tryptophan metabolism toward the kynurenine pathway, leading to L-kynurenine accumulation. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of this pathway significantly alleviates mitochondrial damage, while L-kynurenine supplementation exacerbates injury. Treatment with the IDO inhibitor Epacadostat ameliorates CS-induced lung impairment and inflammation in vivo. These findings define a TALDO1-kynurenine-mitochondrial injury axis linking airway epithelial metabolic reprogramming to COPD, providing translational evidence for targeting this pathway as a therapeutic strategy.

items.title: VAPA-dependent lipid transport at ER-lamellar body contact sites promotes human lung surfactant formation.
items.abstract: Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated proteins (VAPs) establish membrane contact sites (MCS) between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and other organelles through interactions with FFAT-containing proteins, coordinating lipid synthesis, transfer, and metabolism. Their tissue-specific functions remain poorly understood. We report a patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in VAPA (p.(Glu12∗)), presenting with profound global developmental delay and progressive surfactant dysfunction leading to cholesterol pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis. Alternative translation initiation partially bypasses the premature stop codon, producing an N-terminally truncated VAPA protein with impaired FFAT binding capacity and disrupted lamellar body (LB) formation in human alveolar type 2 cells. We identify the pulmonary disease-associated ATP-binding cassette transporter A3 (ABCA3), a regulator of surfactant lipid accumulation, as a VAPA interactor. VAPA-ABCA3 interaction facilitates lipid exchange at previously uncharacterized ER-LB MCSs, a function lost upon VAPA truncation. Our findings establish VAPA-dependent MCS dysfunction as a mechanism of syndromic lung disease and define a pathway for surfactant lipid trafficking.

items.title: Mesothelial plasticity regulates lung mechanical homeostasis in regeneration and fibrosis.
items.abstract: Tissue mechanical adaptation is fundamental to organ development, regeneration, and disease, yet the cellular mechanisms that regulate tissue mechanical adaptation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that mesothelial cells are key regulators of lung mechanical adaptation. Following pneumonectomy, elevated stretch activates YAP (yes-associated protein 1) and induces a transient fibroblast-like mesothelial cell state (F-LMC) characterized by reduced mesothelial identity, increased fibroblast features, and extracellular matrix remodeling at the pleural surface. Yap deletion suppresses F-LMC formation, resulting in lung overinflation and defective regeneration following pneumonectomy. By contrast, in fibrotic lungs, this mesothelial remodeling program is aberrantly activated and restricts lung inflation. Inhibition of this maladaptive response prevents the decline in lung capacity following bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Collectively, our findings redefine the mesothelium as a mechanosensitive regulator of organ-scale mechanical adaptation and reveal how pleural surface remodeling controls tissue mechanics during regeneration and disease.

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles Shed from Senescent Neonatal Pulmonary Microvascular Endothelial Cells Contribute to Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are critical mediators of intercellular communication but their role in bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) complicated by pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) is unclear. Here we test the hypothesis that hyperoxia induces neonatal pulmonary microvascular endothelial cell (PMEC) senescence and that EVs shed from these cells potentiate pulmonary vascular remodeling. Newborn PMECs exposed to 75% O2 had increased expression of senescence markers and young adult rats exposed to neonatal hyperoxia showed increased p16, p21 and p53 expression in pulmonary endothelial cells. In vivo, EVs isolated from the supernatant of senescent PMECs (senescent EVs) induced pulmonary vascular remodelling and PH in newborn rats. miRNA (miR) sequencing revealed 31 differentially expressed miRs in senescent EVs as compared to control EVs. Top upregulated miRs included miR-421, miR-4508, and miR-3960. Senescent EVs differentially regulated 271 genes in the lungs of newborn rats. The most downregulated gene was myocyte enhancer binding factor-2 (MEF2C), a known miR-421 target, involved in smooth cell plasticity. To further interrogate the mechanisms by which senescent EVs induce vascular remodelling, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMs) were incubated with control and senescent EVs, and smooth muscle cell phenotype was assessed. Senescent EVs down-regulated MEF2C and induced a synthetic PASM phenotype. EV uptake inhibition and miR-421 antagomir partially restored MEF2C expression and attenuated these changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that hyperoxia induces PMEC senescence and EVs shed from these senescent cells deliver a miR-421-MEF2C signal that potentiates pulmonary vascular remodelling. Strategies targeting this axis may have important implications for the treatment of BPD-PH.

items.title: LFA-1-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles Deliver CD59 to Protect Endothelial Integrity in Acute Lung Injury.
items.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening disorder characterized by pulmonary endothelial injury, vascular leakage, and hypoxemia, yet no targeted therapies are available to protect the lung vasculature. Dysregulated complement activation contributes to endothelial dysfunction through excessive deposition of the membrane attack complex (MAC), which disrupts endothelial barrier integrity. CD59 is a membrane-bound complement inhibitor that protects endothelial cells (ECs) from MAC-mediated injury, but its role and therapeutic potential in ALI remain unclear. In this study, we found that endothelial CD59 was significantly reduced during bacteria-induced ALI and that Cd59 deficiency exacerbated pulmonary vascular leakage in mice. To supplement endothelial CD59, we engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) expressing lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1) (EVLFA-1) to enhance delivery to activated endothelium. CD59-loaded EVs (EVLFA-1-CD59) preferentially targeted ECs, reduced endothelial MAC deposition and apoptosis, and preserved endothelial barrier integrity in experimental ALI. EVLFA-1-CD59 also improved survival following bacterial infection. Collectively, these data establish diminished endothelial CD59 levels as a critical driver of complement-driven vascular injury and highlight EVLFA-1-mediated CD59 delivery as a promising therapeutic strategy for ALI.

items.title: Molecular imaging of the TGF-β activating integrin αvβ6 detects chronic lung allograft dysfunction.
items.abstract: TGF-β-activating integrins promote solid-organ fibrosis, suggesting their potential as disease markers. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), a progressive fibrotic complication that limits lung transplant survival, is driven by intragraft TGF-β activation. However, TGF-β-activating integrin expression patterns remain undefined in lung transplants. Single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomic analysis of tissue specimens from a mouse CLAD model and human explanted lungs with CLAD revealed high levels of the TGF-β-activating integrin αvβ6, primarily localized to fibrosis-associated Keratin 8+ alveolar transitional epithelial cells, which were greatly reduced in tolerant lungs. Molecular imaging with a newly optimized positron emission tomography radiotracer specific for αvβ6, [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-A20-K16R, showed significantly higher uptake in CLAD than in tolerant transplants. [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-A20-K16R activity was also reduced by experimental treatments that lowered αvβ6 expression and inhibited CLAD severity. Finally, [64Cu]Cu-DOTA-A20-K16R autoradiographic analysis of human explanted lungs with CLAD showed elevated activity that correlated with increased αvβ6 expression. Collectively, these findings illustrate the potential utility of αvβ6 molecular imaging for detecting CLAD pathogenesis.

items.title: RNA-binding proteins as emerging regulators in interstitial lung diseases.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are emerging as critical post-transcriptional regulators that control multiple stages of RNA life cycle, thereby linking post-transcriptional programs to cellular function. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulated RBP-RNA interactions in key pathological mechanisms underlying interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), including epithelial injury, fibroblast activation, immune dysregulation and impaired tissue repair. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), cytoplasmic retention of the RBP Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) in patient derived fibroblasts is associated with preferential binding to profibrotic transcripts, while antisense oligonucleotide mediated suppression of FUS attenuates fibrotic signaling and enhances epithelial regenerative programs in cellular, ex vivo and 3D models. Emerging findings across ILD subtypes suggest that RBP dysregulation may represent a broader post-transcriptional phenomenon. Here, we review the principles governing RBP-RNA interactions, approaches for identifying and measuring these interactions and the links between RBPs, aging and lung pathology. We further discuss the emerging role of RBPs as post-transcriptional orchestrators of ILD pathogenesis and consider their potential as therapeutic targets.

items.title: αTAT1 links microtubules to stiffness sensing, fibroblast activation, and fibrosis.
items.abstract: Matrix stiffening sustains fibrosis by recruiting fibroblasts to stiff fibrotic areas through durotaxis. Once recruited, fibroblasts become mechanically activated and promote scar formation. Although actin-based mechanotransduction and focal adhesion signaling are well established, how microtubules contribute to stiffness sensing and fibroblast activation in fibrosis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify αTAT1-mediated microtubule acetylation as a key regulator of fibroblast mechanosensing, durotaxis, and profibrotic activation. Through α-tubulin K40 acetylation, αTAT1 promotes microtubule flexibility, directional alignment, and persistent polarity along stiffness gradients, thereby enabling stiffness-directed migration and fibroblast activation. Mechanistically, αTAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation regulates focal adhesion dynamics and downstream mechanotransduction. αTAT1 loss abolishes K40 acetylation, impairs FAK-mediated YAP/TAZ signaling, and prevents stiffness- and TGF-β-induced myofibroblast differentiation. Accordingly, global or fibroblast-specific Atat1 depletion reduces fibroblast durotaxis and the accumulation of profibrotic fibroblasts, protecting mice from lung, dermal, and kidney fibrosis without affecting inflammation or vascular integrity. Our findings establish αTAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation as a conserved mechanosensing pathway that links fibroblast durotaxis and activation to fibrosis across organs in vivo, and identify αTAT1 catalytic activity as a potential mechano-therapeutic target in fibrotic disease.

items.title: MUC1 attenuates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease through integrated regulation of pulmonary epithelial cell senescence, transdifferentiation, and inflammatory cascades.
items.abstract: Impaired pulmonary epithelial cell homeostasis is a key pathogenic feature in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mucin 1 (MUC1/Muc1) is a membrane-tethered glycoprotein that plays important roles in modulating various disease progression. This study aims to decipher the role and mechanisms of MUC1 in the pathogenesis of COPD. We found functional variants (rs4072037 T > C and rs12411216 C > A) in MUC1 were associated with increased susceptibility to COPD. MUC1-C expression in lung tissues was age-dependent, elevated in adults but decreased in elderly COPD patients. Aged Muc1-deficient mice showed increased cellular senescence in alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cells and spontaneously developed emphysema. In cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD model mice, Muc1 deficiency caused an accelerated decline in lung function, impaired mitochondrial function, enhanced lung inflammation, and impaired AT2-to- alveolar type I (AT1) epithelial cell transdifferentiation. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated AT2 cell-specific reconstitution of Muc1 ameliorated COPD in association with integrated suppression of pulmonary inflammation and enhancement of AT2 transdifferentiation and mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, we found MUC1 attenuated senescence and associated cell dysfunction, including activation of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy flux and AMPK/NDUFS4-driven mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in AT2 cells. In addition, MUC1 modulated CS extract (CSE)-induced human AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation through enhancement of β-catenin nuclear translocation. Moreover, overexpression of MUC1 in lung epithelial cells inhibited CS-induced NF-κB activation and inflammatory responses in both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, this study identified MUC1 as a protective molecule and potential target for COPD, particularly emphysema, via facilitating AT2-to-AT1 cell transdifferentiation, while prohibiting senescence and inflammation.

items.title: Serine palmitoyltransferase inhibition in SPTSSA-related complex hereditary spastic paraplegia.
items.abstract: Defective feedback inhibition of serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) caused by pathogenic SPTSSA variants underlies childhood-onset complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, yet the developmental timing and therapeutic reversibility of sphingolipid dysregulation remain unclear. We generated a knock-in mouse carrying the disease-associated SptssaT51I variant and show that heterozygous animals exhibit preserved intrinsic SPT activity but impaired ORMDL-mediated regulation, leading to sustained elevation of bioactive sphingolipid intermediates that peak during postnatal myelination. Although gross myelin formation was initially maintained, excess sphingolipid flux rendered oligodendrocytes and neurons selectively vulnerable. Dietary L-serine, which augments SPT substrate availability, amplified sphingolipid accumulation in mutant but not WT mice, unmasking progressive spasticity, axonal injury, myelin ultrastructural defects, and - when administered during early postnatal development - severe pulmonary pathology likely responsible for lethality. Pharmacologic SPT inhibition with myriocin normalized sphingolipid synthesis, prevented serine-induced lethality and reversed neurological and metabolic abnormalities. Translating these findings, treatment of a child with SPTSSA-T51I-associated complex hereditary spastic paraplegia using the FDA-approved SPT inhibitor D-cycloserine resulted in sustained improvement in spasticity, reduced baclofen requirement, and decreased plasma levels of neurofilament light chain (NFL). These data define dysregulated sphingolipid biosynthesis as a developmentally and metabolically sensitive driver of neurodegeneration and suggest SPT inhibition as a mechanistically grounded therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Long-term reprogramming of classical monocytes with altered ontogeny mediates enhanced lung injury in sepsis survivors.
items.abstract: Patients who survive sepsis are predisposed to new hospitalizations for respiratory failure, but the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Using a murine model in which prior sepsis predisposes to enhanced lung injury, we previously discovered that classical monocytes persist in the lungs after long-term recovery from sepsis and exhibit enhanced cytokine expression after secondary challenge with intranasal LPS. Here, we hypothesized that immune reprogramming of post-sepsis monocytes and altered ontogeny predispose to enhanced lung injury. Monocyte depletion and/or adoptive transfer was performed 3 weeks and 3 months after sepsis. Monocytes from post-sepsis mice were necessary and sufficient for enhanced LPS-induced lung injury and promoted neutrophil degranulation. Prior sepsis enhanced JAK/STAT signaling and AP-1 accessibility in monocytes and shifted monocytes toward the neutrophil-like monocyte lineage. Neutrophil-like monocytes demonstrated a proinflammatory phenotype with enhanced IL-1β expression and reduced phagocytic capacity. In human sepsis and/or pneumonia survivors, monocytes were predictive of 90-day mortality and exhibited transcriptional and proteomic neutrophil-like signatures. We conclude that sepsis reprograms monocytes into a proinflammatory phenotype and skews bone marrow progenitors and monocytes toward the neutrophil-like lineage, predisposing them to induce neutrophil degranulation and lung injury.

items.title: SIV infection disrupts the spatial cellular and communication networks of pulmonary granulomas during SIV/Mtb co-infection.
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is the leading infectious cause of death globally. Despite wide use of antiretroviral therapy (ART) by people living with HIV, the risk of TB remains increased. To understand immune interactions within lung granulomas, we compared spatial transcriptomics of Mtb and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) in co-infected macaques with or without ART as a model for HIV/Mtb co-infection. Spatially differentiated transcriptional profiles were observed in Mtb-only granulomas, with myeloid cells enriched in metabolic/antimicrobial pathways within the inner ring and T cell costimulatory/activation pathways enriched in the outer ring. These spatially distinct patterns were lost in SIV/Mtb granulomas, with higher enrichment in type I IFN pathways compared with Mtb-only granulomas. SIV/ART/Mtb granulomas had an intermediate transcriptional pattern without restoration to Mtb-only granulomas, despite a lack of viral replication. Cell-cell communication was reduced among SIV/Mtb co-infected groups. These data suggested that HIV disrupted spatially organized immune functions of granulomas, which were not fully restored by ART.

items.title: Cell-free hemoglobin upregulates pulmonary endothelial heparanase expression to drive glycocalyx destruction and inflammation in sepsis.
items.abstract: Both elevated plasma cell-free hemoglobin (CFH) and heparanase-driven endothelial glycocalyx shedding are contributors to microvascular dysfunction and organ injury in sepsis. However, the mechanisms governing heparanase activation, and the potential role of CFH in this process, are not understood. Utilizing patient samples, mice with cecal slurry-induced (CS-induced) peritonitis and elevated CFH, and human lung microvascular endothelial cells (HLMVECs), we tested the hypothesis that CFH upregulates heparanase production to drive endothelial glycocalyx degradation. In human sepsis, elevated circulating CFH was associated with higher heparanase and heparan sulfate levels, which in turn correlated with adverse clinical outcomes. CS+CFH-treated mice had increased plasma heparanase, glycocalyx degradation, and pulmonary and systemic inflammation; endothelial heparanase deletion abrogated these effects. Additionally, in both pulmonary endothelial cells isolated from CS+CFH-treated mice and HLMVECs exposed to CFH and TNF-α, heparanase transcription and active enzyme production were increased. The deleterious effects of CFH were attenuated by acetaminophen, a hemoprotein reductant. In summary, we demonstrate that CFH oxidation stimulates endothelial heparanase expression and activation during sepsis, leading to endothelial glycocalyx degradation, which may disrupt the endothelial barrier and result in organ injury. Our findings highlight the CFH-heparanase axis as a potential therapeutic target for endothelial glycocalyx preservation in sepsis.

items.title: Sphingolipid metabolism contributes to sexual dimorphism in COPD pathogenesis.
items.abstract: Sex-specific mechanisms in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly defined. Sphingolipids are bioactive mediators that regulate airway epithelial integrity, inflammation, and bronchial smooth muscle tone, and their dysregulation contributes to airway hyperresponsiveness. We tested whether sphingolipid metabolism is regulated by sex in COPD. Lung tissue and paired plasma from female and male never-smoking controls, ever-smoking controls, and individuals with COPD were analyzed for sphingolipid enzyme expression and metabolite levels. Bronchial rings from mice and human bronchial smooth muscle cells (HBSMCs) were exposed to estradiol or cigarette smoke extract (CSE) with and without ceramidase or sphingosine kinase inhibitors. Expression of sphingolipid regulators ASAH1 and ORMDL3 was increased in COPD airways, significantly higher in women, and correlated with airway smooth muscle remodeling. Plasma from women with COPD showed increased sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P), whereas men exhibited higher ceramide levels. Female mice displayed greater CSE-induced bronchial reactivity, attenuated by sphingosine kinase inhibition. In male donor HBSMCs, estradiol increased ASAH1, ORMDL3, S1P, and smooth muscle protein expression and enhanced contractility. CSE further augmented molecular responses in estradiol-treated cells but reduced collagen gel contraction, whereas ceramidase inhibition attenuated estradiol-dependent effects. These findings suggest that estrogen-dependent alterations in sphingolipid metabolism contribute to airway hyperreactivity and remodeling in women with COPD.

items.title: Systemic Inflammation in Bronchiectasis: Data from the EMBARC-BRIDGE Study.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
items.abstract: Neutrophilic inflammation in the airways is associated with exacerbation risk in patients with bronchiectasis. Systemic inflammation and neutrophil function are less characterised. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between systemic inflammation and neutrophil function with severity of disease and clinical outcomes. Observational international multi-centre study of adults with bronchiectasis (EMBARC-BRIDGE). Serum inflammatory profiling was performed in 487 patients using Olink® proteomics, and associations with key clinical and patient reported outcomes, including severe exacerbations during follow-up, were analysed. In a sub-study, peripheral blood neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients and controls were analysed for surface activation and functional markers, and functional responses including degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Systemic inflammatory profiling revealed a dominant neutrophil-endothelial signature. Several proteins including PR3, AZU1, MPO, the soluble IL-33 receptor ST2, and the cellular stress marker GDF-15 were associated with increased disease severity using the bronchiectasis severity index, lower lung function, increased symptoms and for many markers, higher rates of severe exacerbations during follow-up. Neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients exhibited reduced surface CD11b and increased CXCR2, with lower CD11b correlating with lower lung function. Basal degranulation was reduced in bronchiectasis, whereas responsiveness to LPS stimulation was preserved. Bronchiectasis is associated with a systemic neutrophil and endothelial inflammatory signature linked to disease severity and risk of severe exacerbations, alongside altered but functionally-responsive circulating neutrophils.

items.title: Development and Validation of a Pre-COPD Score to Predict Incident COPD.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
items.abstract: The ability to predict progression from a pre-disease state in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pre-COPD, to overt COPD remains limited. To test the hypothesis that development of COPD can be predicted by characterizing pre-COPD and creating a simple pre-COPD score. We identified individuals without airflow obstruction, defined as pre-bronchodilator (BD) forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC)≥0.70 and ≥lower limit of normal, from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS)(N = 14,506), Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS)(N = 8673), and Genetic Epidemiology for COPD (COPDGene) Study(N = 2982). A pre-COPD score was developed in CGPS by assigning 1 point to each of smoking history≥10 pack-years, active smoking, any respiratory symptom, asthma, and pre-BD FEV1/FVC 0.70-0.75, and 4 points for pre-BD FEV1<80% predicted, indicating presence of Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry (PRISm), with external validation in CCHS and COPDGene. Participants were followed for 5-10 years for incident COPD, defined as pre-BD FEV1/FVC<0.70 and FEV1<80% predicted. During follow-up, COPD developed in 669 individuals (4.6%) in CGPS, 685 (7.9%) in CCHS, and 367 (12%) in COPDGene. In CGPS, 10-year incidence was 1.5% in the low-risk, 9.3% in the intermediate-risk, 24% in the high-risk, and 42% in the very high-risk category. Corresponding 5-year incidences were 3.7%, 7.3%, 12%, and 25% in CCHS, and 4.1%, 5.3%, 13%, and 31% in COPDGene, respectively. The pre-COPD score demonstrated good discrimination with areas under curve of 0.88 in CGPS, 0.76 in CCHS, and 0.81 in COPDGene. The pre-COPD score was also associated with exacerbations. The pre-COPD score is useful in predicting the onset of COPD with clinically relevant discrimination in three cohorts with different risk profiles.

items.title: Multimodality Molecular Profiling Nominates Targetable Mechanisms in Progressive RV Dysfunction.
items.abstract: Right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) is a robust predictor of mortality in multiple cardiovascular diseases. Currently, it remains unclear whether the severity of RVD corresponds to distinct cellular and molecular alterations, and this has important implications for defining optimal therapeutic targets. To address this knowledge gap, we performed a multiomic evaluation of pulmonary artery banded pigs with differing degrees of right ventricular (RV) compromise. Pulmonary artery banded pigs were stratified into mild and severe RVD groups based on RV ejection fraction (mild RVD, 38±4%; severe RVD, 20±8%). RV tissue from control, mild RVD, and severe RVD animals was analyzed using single-nucleus RNA sequencing, mitochondrial and cytoplasmic proteomics, and phosphoproteomics. Histological analyses corroborated multiomic findings. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed progressive structural and functional alterations in mild and severe RVD pigs. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing demonstrated that advancing RVD was associated with loss of cardiomyocytes, accumulation of efferocytosis-impaired macrophages, and dysregulated endothelial cells and pericytes. Combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses showed escalating impairments of complex cardiomyocyte metabolism with worsening RVD. RV microvasculature was compromised with severe RVD as there were alterations in endothelial cell/pericyte genetic regulation, colocalization patterns in RV sections, and increased cardiomyocyte HIF1A (hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha) transcript expression. Analysis of both mitochondrial and global proteostasis revealed greater compromise in mitochondrial proteostasis, including downregulation of mitochondrial proteases, chaperones, and ribosomes. Paradoxically, cytoplasmic ribosomes were upregulated in severe RVD. The predicted kinome and phosphatome were uniquely altered in mild RVD as compared with severe RVD. Finally, integration of multiomic approaches identified activation of the ribotoxic stress response, impaired macrophage efferocytosis, and insufficient mitochondrial unfolded protein response as potential contributors to severe RVD. Multispecies comparison suggested that the ribotoxic stress response was the most conserved pathogenic response in RVD. Our multiomic analysis defines the cellular and molecular landscape of progressive RVD and nominates druggable pathways that may promote progressive RVD. Future studies are needed to determine how engaging these pathways influences RV phenotypes.

items.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.
items.abstract: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF. Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations? Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence. PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD. These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

items.title: Alveolar Type II Cell-derived MMP1high basal cells promote destructive microcysts in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
items.abstract: Alveolar microcysts, a hallmark of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), are basal cell (BC)-lined structures that develop near terminal airways and correlate with poor clinical outcomes. Using primary-cell organoids and spatial transcriptomics, we identified striking epithelial similarities between respiratory bronchioles (RBs) and IPF alveolar microcysts, both containing AT0 (ABCA3+/SCGB3A2+), SCGB3A2+, and basaloid/BC populations, although basaloid/BCs were markedly expanded in IPF microcysts. A CEACAM6+ subset of normal RB epithelial cells, termed respiratory airway secretory cells (RASCs), consisted predominantly of SCGB3A2+ cells with only rare BCs (1-5%) that by RNA trajectory analysis suggested BCs arise from SCGB3A2+ progenitors. Accordingly, in organoid cultures nearly all RASC-derived colonies converted to BCs within 9 days, resembling colonies generated by purified BCs. BCs derived from either RASCs or normal alveolar type II (AT2) cells strongly expressed the collagenase matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP1), recapitulating the phenotype of BCs lining IPF microcysts. MMP1high BCs degraded type I collagen ex vivo and generated microcyst-like structures in vivo following xenotransplantation, both abolished by MMP activity inhibition or specific MMP1 deletion by sh-RNAi. Finally, a Frizzled-5 WNT agonist antibody reversed the MMP1high phenotype, identifying AT2- and RB-derived basal cell transdifferentiation as a previously unrecognized driver of alveolar destruction and microcyst formation in IPF and a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: STING engages PKR to drive lysosomal cell death in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury.
items.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) has been implicated in multiple forms of cell death. However, the effector kinases that couple STING to these death programs remain poorly defined. Here, we show that during lung ischemia-reperfusion injury, mitochondrial DNA release engages the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-STING pathway to trigger lysosomal cell death (LCD) in mouse and rat models. In human lung epithelial cells, STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives autophosphorylation of double-stranded RNA-dependent protein kinase (PKR) at serine 33. This phosphorylation of PKR activates IκB kinase-NF-κB signaling independently of the canonical STING-TBK1 and PKR-eIF2α pathways. In turn, NF-κB induces LAMP3 transcription, promoting lysosomal membrane permeabilization and LCD. STING-PKR signaling is also observed in patient-derived lung epithelial cells and alveolar organoids. These findings identify PKR as a non-canonical STING effector and show that blockade of STING-PKR signaling attenuates epithelial LCD and lung injury.

items.title: Eurotransplant experience with model for end-stage liver disease standard exceptions for hepatopulmonary syndrome and portopulmonary hypertension.
items.abstract: This study evaluated outcomes in liver transplantation candidates with a model for end-stage liver disease standard exceptions for hepatopulmonary syndrome and portopulmonary hypertension within Eurotransplant https://bit.ly/4gHaFft

items.title: Paracrine action of bone morphogenetic protein 3 in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
items.abstract: Despite advances in therapy, pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains progressive with poor survival. Although dysregulation of bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signalling is central to PAH, key modulators of this pathway remain incompletely defined. To identify the role of BMP3 in pulmonary vascular homeostasis and PAH. BMP3 expression was assessed in experimental pulmonary hypertension and in pulmonary vascular cells and plasma from PAH patients. In vitro studies were performed in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (hPASMCs) and endothelial cells (hPAECs). Global and smooth muscle cell-specific Bmp3-deficient mice were generated. Recombinant BMP3 and adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) were used to overexpress BMP3 in animal models of PAH. BMP3 is predominantly expressed in PASMCs and is consistently downregulated in experimental and human PAH. Secreted BMP3 from PAH-PASMCs and circulating BMP3 levels in PAH patients were significantly reduced. Functionally, PASMC-derived BMP3 inhibited the migration and proliferation of PAH-diseased PAECs. In both global and smooth muscle cell-specific Bmp3-deficient mice, induction of PAH led to significantly exacerbated disease in middle-aged mice. A recombinant BMP3 prevented and reversed PAH in mice. Furthermore, lung-targeted overexpression of BMP3, via AAV1-BMP3, reversed pulmonary vascular remodelling and ameliorated cardiac function in both mice and rats. Mechanistically, BMP3 restored the balance between BMP/SMAD1,5,8 and transforming growth factor (TGF)-β/SMAD2,3 signalling, and decreased the expression of cell cycle genes in PAECs. BMP3 acts as a paracrine regulator of pulmonary vascular homeostasis and may contribute to the modulation of TGF-β/BMP signalling in PAH, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target.

items.title: ERJ Podcast October 2026: The role of inflammation in the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis.
Exposure to immune stimuli augments alveolar macrophages to acquire neutrophil antimicrobial molecules to prevent bacterial pneumonia.
items.abstract: The protective adaptation of innate immune defenses against respiratory pathogens has been linked to previous exposure to immune stimuli; however, the underlying mechanisms of these adaptations are not yet fully understood. Here, we show that pre-exposure to a low dose of non-specific immune stimuli or infection protects against subsequent lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) challenge. This enhanced protection concurs with increased alveolar macrophages (AMs) resulting from a self-renewal process in the lungs. Importantly, these AMs are programmed to acquire neutrophil-released antimicrobial enzymes from the extracellular space to clear MRSA, prevent tissue damage, and rapidly restore lung homeostasis. AM function depends on differential gene expression, including expression of the efferocytosis receptor Mer proto-oncogene tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and the anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-xL. Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

items.title: Dapagliflozin attenuates progression from prefrailty to frailty in patients with hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
items.abstract: BACKGROUNDChronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension share common pathophysiological pathways contributing to vascular damage, endothelial dysfunction, and physical decline, particularly in older adults with prefrailty. To evaluate the relationship among renal injury, physical performance, and frailty progression in hypertensive older adults with CKD and assess whether dapagliflozin associates with reduced frailty progression, we designed the study DAPA-FORTRESS (DAPAgliflozin and Frailty prOgression in hypeRTension and chRonic kidnEy diSeaSe).METHODSWe enrolled 135 prefrail hypertensive patients with CKD aged >65 years and followed them for 1 year. After coarsened exact matching, our balanced cohort had 105 patients (52 dapagliflozin). Associations between albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and physical performance were analyzed using correlation and regression models. Effect of dapagliflozin on frailty progression was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.RESULTSA significant inverse association between gait speed and albuminuria (r2 = 0.48, P < 0.0001) and significant positive linear association between gait speed and eGFR (r2 = 0.18; P < 0.0001) were observed. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 exhibited significantly worse physical performance than those with higher eGFR (P = 0.0003). In adjusted analyses, receiving dapagliflozin was independently associated with lower odds of progressing to frailty at 1 year (OR = 0.130; CI 0.045-0.381; P < 0.001).CONCLUSIONIn older hypertensive patients with CKD, greater renal injury is associated with worse physical performance, while dapagliflozin use reduces the risk of frailty progression. These findings indicate a potential protective role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in mitigating functional decline in this high-risk population.FUNDINGNIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (R01-HL146691), National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (R01-DK123259); American Heart Association (AHA- 24IPA1268813, AHA-22-915561, AHA-24-1195524).

items.title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
items.abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

items.title: Biallelic loss-of-function PTPN6 variants lead to inflammatory lung disease and hemolytic anemia.
items.abstract: Severe inflammatory lung disease, including acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), is life-threatening with diverse causes and few targeted therapies. Inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) underlie a subset of cases. We describe a novel IEI caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in PTPN6, encoding the immunoregulatory phosphatase SHP1. Seven children from five families developed early-onset anemia and severe inflammatory lung disease, at times presenting as ARDS. The causative variants were shown to destabilize SHP1 and abolish its phosphatase activity. These findings expand the genetic landscape of inflammatory lung disease and suggest SHP1 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy for immune-mediated pulmonary pathology.

items.title: Evaluation of Andes virus vaccine-derived human antibody for protection in Syrian hamsters: a passive transfer study using phase 1 trial sera.
items.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) causes severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and is uniquely capable of person-to-person transmission, with no licenced vaccines or therapeutics available. A Phase 1 trial (NCT03682107) demonstrated that an ANDV DNA vaccine targeting Gn/Gc envelope proteins elicits neutralising antibodies in humans. We evaluated whether these human antibodies protect against lethal disease in an animal model. Day 197 sera from vaccinated human subjects were pooled, purified, and passively transferred to female Syrian hamsters one day prior to lethal ANDV challenge across two independent experiments. Controls included normal human IgG, PBS (negative controls), and SAB-400 (positive control). Neutralising antibody levels were quantified using pseudovirion neutralisation assays (PsVNA) and plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT) to determine exploratory cutoff titres predicting survival. Human antibodies from DNA-vaccinated subjects-unlike normal IgG-conferred significant protection against lethal ANDV challenge in both experiments. The exploratory cutoff titres predicting protection were determined to be 31-184 for PsVNA50 and 20-80 for PRNT50, depending on the analysis population and model parameters. Vaccine-induced human antibodies are sufficient to protect against lethal ANDV infection in an established animal model. If confirmed, these results indicate that neutralising antibody titres could serve as a surrogate endpoint and correlate of protection for future hantavirus Gn/Gc-targeted vaccines. Defense Health Program and the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

items.title: Human adult and pediatric multimodal transcriptomic atlas of progression from pressure-loaded to failing right ventricle.
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) independently predicts mortality in heart failure, yet its pathophysiology is poorly understood. Here we present a multi-modal atlas of human right ventricular pressure loading and failure, including bulk (n = 142), single-nucleus (n = 11) and Xenium spatial (n = 9) transcriptomics in adults, plus pediatric (n = 14) and mouse pulmonary artery banding cohorts. Subclustering resolved 34 cell subtypes across 12 lineages along a two-phase trajectory. Phase 1 (non-failing to pressure-loaded) accounts for most of the transcriptional change detectable by bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing and is marked by loss of resident macrophage identity, fibroblast activation, endothelial expansion and erosion of tissue-protective programs. Phase 2 (pressure-loaded to RVF) produces little change in bulk RNA sequencing but is resolved by spatial transcriptomics, engaging multi-lineage fibrotic, endothelial-activation and cardiomyocyte-reactivation programs, with a gain of extracellular matrix (collagen, laminin, thrombospondin) signaling over a stable cell contact adhesion baseline. Mitochondrial respirometry revealed respiratory dysfunction in adult and mouse RVF but not pediatric RVF. Multi-lineage remodeling of the cardiac microenvironment emerges as the central molecular program of RVF, meriting further study as possible disease-modifying targets.

items.title: Alveolar stem cells transdifferentiate to drive bronchiolar regeneration.
items.abstract: The lung consists of two anatomically distinct compartments: the airways and the alveoli. Although airway epithelial stem cells are known to mobilize for alveolar regeneration, whether alveolar cells can reciprocally traverse these anatomical boundaries and contribute to bronchial repair remains unclear1-4. Here we developed dual-recombinase-mediated lineage-tracing techniques in mice to demonstrate that alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells migrate into injured bronchioles and transdifferentiate into club cells and ciliated cells, thereby actively contributing to airway regeneration. Mechanistically, after bronchial injury, infiltrating immune cells secrete SPP1, establishing a chemotactic gradient directing cell migration. Peribronchiolar AT2 cells sense this SPP1 signal through the integrin ITGB1 and migrate towards the injured bronchioles. On arrival, these migrated AT2 cells receive Notch ligands from resident ciliated cells, leading to Notch pathway activation, which in turn drives their transdifferentiation into club cells. This transdifferentiation process is accompanied by an intermediate stage marked by Cldn4 expression. Functional blockade of either SPP1 or ITGB1 impairs AT2 cell migration, whereas inhibition of Notch signalling prevents their transdifferentiation into club cells. Collectively, our findings reveal a cross-compartmental cellular mechanism for bronchiolar epithelial repair, expanding the current understanding of lung regenerative plasticity and potentially informing therapeutic strategies for airway injury.

items.title: All-fiber wireless auscultation garment for cardiopulmonary diagnostics.
items.abstract: Daily apparel could enable continuous, noninvasive monitoring of cardiopulmonary health for the early detection and treatment of cardiopulmonary diseases, the leading causes of death and disability worldwide. Here we develop an all-fiber wireless auscultation system seamlessly integrated into garments. An ~150-μm-diameter fiber contact microphone is sewn, knitted or woven into clothing to capture deep-body acoustic signals while overcoming acoustic impedance mismatch and electromagnetic noise. An ~500-μm knitted fiber computer enables real-time signal processing and Bluetooth transmission to a mobile device. A clinical study in 10 patients with heart failure and 20 neonates demonstrated cardiopulmonary sound capture, including qualitative examples of pathological acoustic features such as cardiac murmurs, S3 gallops and crackles. Comparative validation against a digital stethoscope confirms the garment's ability to suppress environmental noise for high-fidelity cardiopulmonary sound capture. In addition, the fiber integrated within the garment array enables spatial sound mapping of cardiac and pulmonary abnormalities for localized diagnostics.

items.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa induces the generation of pathogenic IFNγ+Th17 cells that promote lung damage and chronic inflammation in cystic fibrosis.
items.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) involves cycles of bacterial infection and sustained inflammation. IFNγ+Th17 cells are implicated in chronic inflammation, yet their role in CF remains undefined. Here we identify two pathogenic Th17 subsets, Th1/17+ and pro-inflammatory Th17 (pTh17) cells, selectively enriched in CF lungs colonized by Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These pathogenic subsets derive from protective conventional Th17 (cTh17) precursors and, following activation, directly disrupt pulmonary epithelial integrity and trigger exaggerated inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic and T cell receptor profiling reveal in situ reprogramming and clonal selection of Th1/17+ and pTh17 cells in CF lungs. Mechanistically, clinical P. aeruginosa strains persist within dendritic cells and induce a polarizing IL-1β/IL-23 cytokine axis that promotes IFNγ+Th17 differentiation over classical Th1 lineage commitment. P. aeruginosa early isolates, lacking chronic adaptation signatures, still potently reprogramme cTh17 cells, inducing a transcriptional programme that mirrors CF lung-resident Th1/17+ and pTh17 profiles. These findings show that P. aeruginosa subverts mucosal immunity and establishes a self-sustaining immunopathological loop, offering potential targets for CF precision therapies.

items.title: State-level burden of chronic respiratory diseases in the USA, 1990-2023, with forecasts to 2050: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
items.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases are a leading cause of mortality in the USA, with considerable regional disparities influenced by environmental, occupational, and behavioural risk factors. This study aimed to quantify levels of, and trends in, the burden of chronic respiratory diseases in the USA from 1990 to 2023, with estimates of prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs); identify risk factors contributing to this burden; and project prevalence trends until 2050. Using data from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023, we estimated the disease burden for four types of chronic respiratory disease: asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pneumoconiosis, and interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary sarcoidosis. Estimates were stratified by age group, sex, and year from 1990 to 2023, along with corresponding 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Furthermore, we examined total percentage change before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, and forecast the future burden of chronic respiratory diseases through 2050. In 2023, an estimated 54·50 million (95% UI 48·86-61·60) individuals lived with chronic respiratory disease in the USA, compared with 33·28 million (28·61-38·23) in 1990. The age-standardised prevalence rate increased by 10·24% (8·01-12·47) between 1990 and 2023, while the age-standardised mortality rate rose modestly from 31·19 (28·85-32·95) per 100 000 population to 34·56 (30·64-37·89) per 100 000 population, indicating persistent gaps in disease control. Marked geographical variation was observed, with the highest age-standardised mortality rates due to COPD and pneumoconiosis in Appalachian states (eg, Kentucky and West Virginia) and elevated asthma and ILD burden in the southern and Great Plains regions. Modifiable risk factors accounted for 44·54% (41·71-45·74) of total DALYs due to chronic respiratory diseases, driven mainly by high BMI for asthma, smoking for COPD, and occupational exposure to asthmagens for pneumoconiosis. Across the US states, higher cigarette taxation and broader respiratory infection vaccination coverage were linked to lower age-standardised DALY rates for COPD and ILD and pulmonary sarcoidosis, whereas asthma showed no consistent pattern. According to our projection models, by 2050, 45·72 million (28·96-67·27) individuals in the USA will have asthma, while 19·61 million (16·70-22·26) will have COPD, 1·05 million (0·74-1·44) will have ILD and pulmonary sarcoidosis, and 0·01 million (0·008-0·02) will have pneumoconiosis. State-level policy environments, including fiscal and preventive health measures, might contribute to shaping respiratory health outcomes beyond individual risk factors. Integrating tobacco control measures, equitable vaccination programmes, and targeted health-system investments could help to address the uneven burden of chronic respiratory diseases across US states and the growing mortality gap despite stable prevalence, although further research is needed to clarify which specific policy determinants underlie these associations. Gates Foundation.

items.title: IL-17A-producing γδ T cells control pulmonary Mycobacterium abscessus infection in mice.
items.abstract: The specific role of γδ T cells in non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infections remains incompletely understood. Here we characterized the immune landscape of pulmonary tissues from a Mycobacterium abscessus-infected NTM mice model. Interleukin-17 (IL-17)A+ γδ T cells were essential for controlling M. abscessus infection by directly eliminating extracellular bacteria. These cells conferred protective immunity in two mouse models of infection combined with either pulmonary fibrosis or a lack of functional interferon-gamma (IFNγ)-mediated immunity. IL-17A+ γδ T cells exerted bactericidal activity via granzyme B-dependent cytotoxic pathways. Absence of IL-17A substantially impaired bacterial recognition and cytotoxic function of IL-17A+ γδ T cells, highlighting the cell-intrinsic requirement for IL-17A signalling in γδ T cell activation. M. abscessus recognition through Toll-like receptor 2 induced macrophage production of IL-1β and IL-23, promoting the expansion and activation of IL-17A+ γδ T cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing on human peripheral blood mononuclear cells suggests that anti-IFNγ autoantibodies compromise γδ T cell function. Our findings establish IL-17A+ γδ T cells as a promising therapeutic target for NTM infections, particularly when IFNγ-dependent immunity is compromised.

items.title: Population-based Prevalence of Bronchiectasis in the United States.
items.abstract: Bronchiectasis is a chronic, heterogeneous lung disease of rising prevalence; however, contemporary epidemiological data are lacking. Furthermore, paediatric prevalence and cystic fibrosis (CF)-related bronchiectasis prevalence are frequently absent from existing literature. What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States? This retrospective, observational study utilised data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart claims database to estimate the age- and sex-standardised prevalence of bronchiectasis in the US in people of all ages and paediatrics (aged <18 years). Prevalence was stratified by age, sex, ethnicity and insurance coverage. Individuals were required to have ≥1 day of enrolment during the index period (2018-2022); the index date was the latest day in this period with ≥365 days of prior continuous enrolment. In the overall population, 94,392 cases of bronchiectasis were identified (median age, 76 years). Five-year prevalence was 221.6 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 220.1-223.1) per 100,000 persons and increased with age. Prevalence was higher among females (274.6 per 100,000 persons), Asians (302.3 per 100,000 persons) and Medicare Advantage enrolees (528.6 per 100,000 persons). In total, 1.4% of the overall population had a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. Five-year prevalence in the paediatric population (including 465 cases; median age, 12 years) was 11.9 (95% CI: 10.8-13.1) per 100,000 persons. Paediatric prevalence was similar between sexes, higher in Caucasians and higher in those with non-CF-related bronchiectasis than CF-related bronchiectasis. This current study reports that bronchiectasis prevalence continues to increase in the US compared with previous studies, with a consistently higher prevalence in females and Asians, and that a lower proportion of individuals have CF-related bronchiectasis compared with non-CF-related bronchiectasis.

items.title: Lung Allograft Function After Primary Graft Dysfunction in the Lung Transplant Outcomes Group Cohort.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
items.abstract: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplant is associated with increased mortality. Whether PGD increases mortality via long-term effects on allograft function is poorly understood. Evaluate the association of PGD with potential lung function and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). We included lung transplant recipients enrolled in an 8-center prospective cohort study from 2007-2018. PGD was defined by ISHLT criteria. Linear mixed effects and logistic regression models evaluated the association between PGD and maximum potential forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) and whether Global Lung Function Initiative defined (GLI) predicted FEV1 was attained, respectively. Flexible parametric survival models evaluated the association between PGD and CLAD, accounting for confounding and mortality as a competing risk. Among 2419 recipients, 510 had PGD. Recipients with PGD had lower maximum potential FEV1 (-311 ml, 95% CI -245 to -377 ml) and were less likely to achieve GLI-predicted FEV1 (probability difference -12.5%, 95% CI -17 to -8%). 930 recipients developed CLAD (405 obstructive, 525 restrictive) over median (IQR) 5.9 (3.0-8.0 years). The 5-year cumulative incidence of CLAD did not differ by PGD (cumulative difference: -2.2%, 95% CI - 6.4% to 1.9%). This association was not modified by age, sex, BMI, pretransplant diagnosis, or transplant type. PGD was not associated with a difference in cumulative incidence of obstructive or restrictive CLAD (cumulative difference -1.2% and -0.8%, respectively). PGD is associated with reduced lung function and lower likelihood of achieving GLI-predicted maximum potential lung function but not CLAD.

items.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections.
items.abstract: Host resistance to infection is initially determined by how well primed the innate immune system is to respond on first exposure to an invader, yet the mechanisms underlying this priming remain incompletely understood. Here we found that basal autophagy suppressed the expression of Il1a in alveolar macrophages (AMs) and an otherwise protective innate immune priming against Staphylococcus aureus and influenza A virus (IAV), independently of the microbiome and adaptive immunity. Inactivating autophagy genes in AMs led to elevated expression of IL-1α in AMs, which subsequently enhanced IL-1R-MyD88 signaling in neutrophils and increased the recruitment of myeloid cells to the lung. As a result, autophagy-deficient mice showed more efficient clearance of S. aureus along with reduced lung damage and inflammation. Similar to genetic inactivation of autophagy, overexpression of IL-1α in AMs conferred broad spectrum protection against S. aureus and IAV, suggesting a possible strategy to fine-tune immune responses to combat important respiratory infections.

items.title: Muco-obstructive lung disease exhibits distinct hypoxic and inflammatory airway epithelial gene pathways.
items.abstract: Intraluminal obstruction produces chronic airway epithelial hypoxia. We investigated how chronic airway epithelial hypoxia and inflammatory stimuli interact in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cultures and resected human bronchiectatic lungs to produce an airway epithelial environment characteristic of muco-obstructive disease. HBE cultures were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (1% O2) for 5 days, followed by administration of supernatants from cystic fibrosis (CF) lung-derived mucopurulent material (SMM) or PBS for 24 h. A reverse order protocol with SMM followed by hypoxia was also performed. Bulk RNA-sequencing and functional (Na+ transport) studies were performed. HIF1A and EPAS1-mediated transcriptional responses were characterised in CRISPR knockdown HBE cells. RNA in situ hybridisation studies of excised bronchiectatic lungs and bioinformatic analyses of published datasets tested for relevance of in vitro findings to in vivo conditions. Hypoxia and SMM regulated largely separate airway epithelial transcriptional programmes regardless of treatment order. PTGS2 (COX-2), CCL20, MUC5B, and CXCL8 (IL-8) represented a small number of genes upregulated by both hypoxia and SMM. HIF1A knockdown and EPAS1 knockdown produced distinct, often opposing, effects on hypoxia-responsive pathways. HIF1A dominated upregulation of glycolytic pathway signalling. EPAS1 regulated genes that increase mucus concentration under hypoxia (e.g., SCNN1G). An EPAS1 inhibitor blocked hypoxia-induced upregulation of Na+ transport. Chronic hypoxia and inflammation regulated distinct genes/pathways that combine to produce a complex diseased environment in muco-obstructed airway epithelia. HIF1A and EPAS1 regulated distinct hypoxia-induced transcriptional responses. EPAS1 inhibition may exhibit a favourable therapeutic ratio for treatment of muco-obstructive lung diseases.

items.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome FXR/Sptlc2 signaling promotes alveolar macrophage mitophagy and limits lung inflammation.
items.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) undergo functional reprogramming that critically regulates lung inflammation. Although mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control, its role in macrophage functional reprogramming during acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Nr1h4 (FXR) as a transcriptional regulator of mitophagy in AMs. FXR activation transcriptionally upregulates serine palmitoyltransferase long chain base subunit 2 (Sptlc2), thereby enhancing mitophagy and promoting an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype under inflammatory conditions. The FXR/Sptlc2 axis reduces oxidative stress and inflammatory mediator production while increasing anti-inflammatory markers. Conversely, FXR deficiency impairs mitophagy, exacerbates pulmonary inflammation, and aggravates lung injury in vivo. These findings establish the FXR/Sptlc2 axis as a regulator of mitochondrial quality control and macrophage functional reprogramming and identify it as a potential therapeutic target in ARDS.

items.title: 17β-Estradiol and Estrogen Receptor α Promote Right Ventricle Angiogenesis in Pulmonary Hypertension via Apelin Signaling.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) failure is the major cause of mortality in pulmonary hypertension (PH). Adaptive angiogenesis and RV endothelial cell (RVEC) function are major modifiers of RV adaptation in PH, but the underlying mechanisms and their regulators remain incompletely understood. RV adaptation in PH is sexually dimorphic, and 17β-estradiol (E2) exerts protective effects on RV cardiomyocytes. Whether E2 modifies angiogenesis and RVEC function in RV failure remains unknown. We hypothesized that E2 and estrogen receptor α (ERα) promote RV angiogenesis and RVEC homeostasis in PH and aimed to identify underlying mechanisms. We assessed E2's angiogenic effects using cultured human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMVECs), RVECs from PH patients with RV failure, and RVECs from sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) and monocrotaline rat models. In vivo, we evaluated RV capillary density in PH rats treated with E2 or ERα-selective agonist. Apelin signaling was evaluated via apelin receptor (APLNR) blockade and knockdown studies. E2 preserved angiogenesis in male hCMVECs and RV capillary density in male and female SuHx-PH rats. E2 reversed angiogenic alterations in RVECs from SuHx-PH rats via APLNR signaling. In RVECs from RV failure patients, E2 stimulated vascular network formation. In rat and human PH-RVECs, ERα was necessary and sufficient to mediate E2-induced angiogenesis. Activation of ERα with ERα-specific agonist restored RV capillary density in vivo. ERα-mediated angiogenesis required apelin signaling. These data indicate that E2 promotes RV angiogenesis via ERα and apelin signaling and identify a novel ERα-apelin axis in RVECs as a potential therapeutic target to restore RV vascular integrity in PH.

items.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory.
items.abstract: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1-7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

items.title: MUC5B Overproduction Disrupts Club Cell Mediated Alveolar Repair in COPD.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by small airway disease (SAD) and emphysema, but mechanisms linking these pathologies remain unclear. SAD arises early and is the primary site of airflow limitation, marked by epithelial injury, mucus obstruction, and bronchiole loss. Excessive production of the mucin MUC5B by bronchiolar club cells is a key feature of SAD and is associated with impaired mucociliary clearance and inflammation. Club cells also function as progenitors for alveolar type II (ATII) cells, yet how their regenerative capacity is altered in COPD is unknown. To determine whether MUC5B overproduction in small airway club cells alters their capacity to regenerate ATII cells and contributes to emphysema progression. We assessed MUC5B expression in human emphysematous lungs and a porcine pancreatic elastase (PPE)-induced mouse model of emphysema. Genetic approaches were used to overexpress or conditionally delete Muc5b in club cells to evaluate effects on club-to-ATII differentiation, alveolar structure, and lung function in health and emphysema. MUC5B is overexpressed in small airway club cells in human emphysematous lungs and animal models. Muc5b overexpression impairs differentiation of club cells into ATII cells and worsened lung function decline in emphysema. Importantly, conditional deletion of Muc5b during early disease stages restored club cell-derived alveolar regeneration. MUC5B overproduction links SAD to defective alveolar repair by limiting club cell progenitor function. Targeting MUC5B may restore epithelial regeneration and slow early COPD progression.
