items.title: Natural Killer Cell TGF-β Signaling Regulates Postnatal Lung Development.
items.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a disease of neonatal lung development that is linked to impaired pulmonary vascularization, dysregulated TGF-β (transforming growth factor-β) signaling, and the accumulation of senescent cells. Despite the established role of TGF-β signaling in promoting vascular remodeling and suppressing the senolytic activity of natural killer (NK) cells, the contribution of NK cell TGF-β signaling to postnatal lung patterning and the pathogenesis of BPD remains unclear. Mice bearing an NK cell-selective deletion of the type-II TGF-β receptor (Tgfbr2NK-/-) were analyzed for vascular and alveolar structure, lung NK cell infiltration, senescence markers, and lung function testing across neonatal and adult time points. Lung tissue from both neonatal mice and human infants with BPD was assessed by single-cell RNA sequencing. The effects of enhanced NK cell activity in a hyperoxia-induced model of BPD were examined in Tgfbr2NK-/- neonates, as well as pharmacologically, using the TGF-β ligand trap/IL-15 superagonist, HCW9218. Neonatal Tgfbr2NK-/- mice exhibited a baseline reduction in distal arteriolar density, impaired alveolarization, and sex-specific deficits in long-term lung function. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified excessive clearance of senescent endothelial cells by TGF-β-insensitive NK cells in the lungs of Tgfbr2NK-/- neonates. This enhanced NK cell activity promoted a BPD-like phenotype in naïve Tgfbr2NK-/- mice but protected these animals from impaired lung development under hyperoxia. Sequencing of lung tissue from human infants with BPD confirmed excessive TGF-β signaling and cytotoxic impairment in NK cells. Treatment with HCW9218 prevented senescent cell accumulation and rescued lung development in the hyperoxia mouse model. TGF-β is a tunable regulator of NK cell senolytic activity that is essential for normal postnatal lung development. Excessive NK cell TGF-β signaling contributes to impaired lung development with neonatal hyperoxia and may serve as a viable therapeutic target in human BPD.

items.title: Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut-lung axis.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
items.abstract: Respiratory infections remain a major global health challenge, further compounded by antibiotic resistance. Among these, mycoplasmal pneumonia represents a particularly prevalent and refractory form. Here, using targeted enzymatic fragmentation combined with multidimensional NMR analysis, we resolved the structure of a homogeneous Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide, GLFP2, and identified β-(1→6)-linked galactosyl motifs as key structural features. Despite minimal systemic absorption, oral GLFP2 alleviated mycoplasmal pneumonia in mice. Instead, GLFP2 reshaped the gut microbiota and functionally reprogrammed gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs), whose transplantation alone was sufficient to confer pulmonary protection. Orally administered GMEVs remained bioactive, showed systemic exposure, associated with the lung, and were preferentially taken up by alveolar macrophages. These vesicles activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, suppressed the S100A8/A9 inflammatory axis, and limited neutrophil-driven immunopathology. Collectively, these findings identify microbiota-derived vesicles as effectors of gut-lung communication and use a defined polysaccharide to uncover a remote protective mechanism against pneumonia.

items.title: Histone lactylation regulates macrophage polarization and metabolic homeostasis during hypoxic lung injury.
items.abstract: The M1-to-M2 macrophage phenotypic switch is critical for resolving inflammation and restoring homeostasis in hypoxic lung injury, but the underlying molecular mechanisms are unclear. Here, we show that hypoxia-induced histone lactylation (Kla) upregulates FTO via HIF1a-P300 interaction; lactylation-driven FTO then promotes late-stage M2 polarization by stabilizing Arg1 mRNA through the m6A-YTHDF2 axis. Mechanistically, HIF1a/YY1 liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates macrophage glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) via the cGAS-STING pathway downstream of lactylation. Importantly, lactylation exerts context-dependent dual effects: physiological lactylation in wild-type mice facilitates M2 polarization, maintains metabolic balance, and promotes lung repair, whereas excessive lactylation in IL-10-deficient mice disrupts the FTO-Arg1 cascade, perturbs metabolism, blocks M2 polarization, and aggravates injury. Collectively, histone lactylation is a core switch governing macrophage polarization and metabolic homeostasis in hypoxic lung injury, with its function dictated by IL-10 status and lactylation abundance.

items.title: Processing of lysophosphatidylcholines by ExoU secreted by P. aeruginosa leads to inflammasome activation and cell death.
items.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) thrives in the lungs of patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) which results in pulmonary inflammation and decline in lung function. Inflammasome signaling promotes host cell death and processing of IL-1 which results in bacterial control. Since the type 3 secretion system (T3SS) of P. aeruginosa induces inflammasome signaling, we evaluated the role of ExoU, a phospholipase which is secreted through the T3SS and promotes host susceptibility. Our results indicate that the genes associated with T3SS-function display increased polymorphism and are poorly expressed in the chronic isolates of P. aeruginosa from patients with CF, which leads to poor inflammasome activation. ExoU, secreted by P. aeruginosa modulates the lipidome of infected cells extensively, which results in an increase in the intracellular levels of lysophosphatidylcholine species that leads to the activation of NF-κB and MAPK pathways and cell death by inflammasome signaling, which is inhibited by lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 3 (LPCAT3).

items.title: ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis.
items.abstract: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis. ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2-modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF. In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

items.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
items.abstract: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined. To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH. Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models. In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models. The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

items.title: CCR2-Dependent Myeloid Cell Recruitment Links Post-MI Heart Failure to Pulmonary Hypertension.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is a common complication of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). Myeloid inflammation is a major hallmark of both the local cardiac and systemic post-MI response, with resident and recruited monocyte-derived macrophages orchestrating each step of the ensuing inflammatory cascade, from clearance of dead cardiomyocytes to scar tissue formation. Similarly, myeloid inflammation is a key feature of the PH lung, driving remodeling of small pulmonary vessels. We thus hypothesized that MI-induced systemic myeloid inflammation contributes directly to the development of PH-LHD. We assessed expression of inflammatory adhesion molecules, as markers of vascular inflammatory activation and myeloid cell recruitment pathways, in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, PH-LHD, as well as in a PH-LHD rat model. We then induced MI and subsequent HF in 8- to 10-week-old female C57BL/6J mice via permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. HF mice were then treated with a CCR2 (C-C chemokine receptor 2) antagonist to block monocyte recruitment and the development of PH-LHD was assessed at 6 weeks post-MI by a combination of invasive hemodynamics, flow cytometry, echocardiography, and lung histology. Expression of key inflammatory adhesion molecules, including VCAM1 and SELE, was increased in PH-LHD lungs from humans and rats. Following early post-MI development of HF with reduced ejection fraction, mice exhibited increased numbers of circulating monocytes, lung monocytes, and lung interstitial macrophages, as well as PH-LHD by 6 weeks, characterized by right ventricular hypertrophy, elevated right ventricular pressures, and lung vascular remodeling of small-to-medium-sized pulmonary vessels. Administration of the selective CCR2 antagonist RS102895 from day 10 post-MI to reduce monocyte tissue recruitment attenuated lung vascular remodeling, right ventricular systolic and diastolic pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and lung adhesion molecule expression at 6 weeks, compared with vehicle-treated controls, without improving the underlying left-sided HF. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

items.title: Identification of a Novel EBF1-Expressing Disease-Associated Arterial Subpopulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
items.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating disease with a poor prognosis. However, only a limited number of palliative interventions are currently available. To address this unmet need, it is essential to understand the molecular causes of PAH by identifying unique disease-associated populations and their key molecular regulators during disease progression. We constructed a single-cell multiome data set at 4 distinct time points during the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) using endothelial cells isolated from the Sugen5416/hypoxia rat model. We assessed the conservation of novel disease-associated endothelial cells by reanalyzing previously reported single-cell RNA sequencing data from human patients with PAH. We validated the functional importance of EBF1 (early B-cell factor 1) in PAH by performing in silico simulations and an in vivo knockdown mediated by a pulmonary endothelium-targeting associated virus. We found that PH progression gradually altered the transcriptional and epigenetic landscape of the pulmonary endothelium in a stage-specific manner, leading to the emergence of a novel disease-associated arterial endothelial population expressing EBF1. A similar endothelial subset was present in human patients with PAH. Immunofluorescence revealed that EBF1 expression was elevated in both human and rat lungs during PH progression. In silico simulations suggested that EBF1 is required for the pathogenic state, and the associated virus-mediated in vivo knockdown of Ebf1 ameliorated the pathological hallmarks of PH, including right ventricular systolic pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, when delivered either before the onset of PH or after its establishment. We identified EBF1 as a key transcriptional regulator of a novel disease-associated population in both humans and rats. We further demonstrated that inhibiting EBF1 within the pulmonary endothelium ameliorates the pathological features of PH, suggesting that EBF1 and its transcriptional targets represent a novel and promising therapeutic avenue for PAH.

NAD+ metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease.
items.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

items.title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment.
items.abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor-mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

items.title: Pathogenic B-T Cell Axis Driven by BAFF Induces Endothelial Apoptosis in SLE-PAH.
items.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a fatal complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), yet the mechanisms linking autoimmune dysregulation to progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling are poorly defined, leading to inadequate therapies. This study investigated BAFF (B-cell activating factor), a key cytokine in SLE, as a potential driver of SLE-PAH pathogenesis. BAFF expression was assessed in patients with SLE-PAH and animal models. Humanized BAFF-transgenic mice were generated to investigate the effects of BAFF elevation on serological, hemodynamic, and histological parameters of SLE and PAH. Single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, histological analyses, and cell-based experiments were performed to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms. The therapeutic efficacy of the BAFF-neutralizing antibody Belimumab was tested in 2 distinct SLE-PAH animal models. BAFF was significantly upregulated in both SLE-PAH patient cohorts and animal models. Humanized BAFF-transgenic mice exhibited systemic B-cell hyperactivation and pulmonary infiltration and spontaneously developed hallmark features of both SLE and PAH. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of lung tissues revealed that BAFF overexpression drove the increase of a novel, disease-specific S100a6+ mature B-cell subset, which orchestrated a pathogenic immune cascade by activating a cytotoxic Gzmk+ CD8+ T-cell population via MHC-I (major histocompatibility complex class I)-mediated antigen presentation and CD80-CD28 costimulation. This B-T cell crosstalk triggered apoptosis of a susceptible endothelial cell subpopulation through Fas/Fas ligand signaling, ultimately culminating in pulmonary vascular remodeling. The BAFF-neutralizing antibody Belimumab effectively ameliorated both autoimmune and cardiopulmonary manifestations in 2 distinct SLE-PAH animal models, while improving survival. These findings establish BAFF as a key mediator in SLE-PAH, driving a previously unrecognized pathogenic immune axis connecting dysregulated B cells to T-cell-mediated endothelial injury. BAFF inhibition may represent a therapeutic strategy for SLE-PAH.

items.title: Diagnostic Contribution of Endobronchial Optical Coherence Tomography in the Multidisciplinary Diagnosis of Interstitial Lung Disease.
items.abstract: Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB. How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC? Patients with low-confidence ILD diagnosis clinically referred for both TBLC with EGC were enrolled to undergo concurrent EB-OCT imaging. Each modality was interpreted independently by blinded pathologists. Separate MDD sessions were conducted at two independent sites, including one without prior EB-OCT experience. Fifteen patients were included (9 male; mean age: 70.6 years) with final diagnoses of UIP/IPF (n=5), secondary UIP (n=2), and various non-UIP ILDs (n=8) in agreement at both MDDs. EB-OCT provided diagnostic data that was in agreement with final MDD diagnosis for 100% of subjects (15/15), including in the 40% of subjects (6/15) where TBLC was non-diagnostic. In the subjects where TBLC yielded diagnostic data (60%, 9/15), EB-OCT diagnosis was in agreement. EB-OCT combined with TBLC/EGC increased diagnostic confidence and/or narrowed the differential diagnosis from baseline clinical/radiologic data review in all subjects, with replication across both independent MDDs. In this pilot study, we demonstrate EB-OCT is a safe, large-volume imaging method that detects microscopic features and patterns for ILD diagnosis, which increases diagnostic confidence in the context of MDD and complements TBLC and EGC. Future multicenter studies are needed to further validate these findings.

items.title: Targeting ZIP12-mediated Zn2+ signaling as a treatment for pulmonary hypertension.
items.abstract: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12, ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Defining GRAMD2 expression in the alveolar epithelium using organoid and single cell approaches.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Alveolar epithelial regeneration is critical for normal lung function and disrupted in disease. Precise identification of alveolar epithelial cell populations, particularly type I (AT1) cells, remains a barrier to understanding alveolar homeostasis and repair. We previously identified GRAM domain-containing 2 (GRAMD2) as enriched in distal alveolar epithelium, with predominant expression in type I (AT1) cells. However, recent single-cell datasets reveal low level Gramd2 transcripts in other lung epithelial populations raising questions about specificity. To address this, we performed immunofluorescence of whole lung and cytospins of GFPhigh cells from Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice. Cre-induced lineage labeling predominantly marked cells expressing established AT1 markers, with minimal labeling of AT2 or club cells. GFPhigh cells were enriched for AT1 cells and formed organoids in culture that over time showed expression of AT2 and airway markers, suggesting plasticity. Despite apparent purity of the GFPhigh population by immunostaining, single-cell RNAseq identified AT2 cells and a small number of club cells in the labeled population, revealing discordance between GRAMD2 transcript and protein expression. Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice enable enrichment of AT1 cells but have limitations for definitive lineage tracing.

items.title: The impact of modulator therapy on the Pseudomonas aeruginosa cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
items.abstract: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts P. aeruginosa physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that P. aeruginosa lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of P. aeruginosa transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate P. aeruginosa gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with Staphylococcus aureus had limited effects. These findings show that ETI therapy has little impact on the conserved P. aeruginosa transcriptional state in human CF sputum and that refined sputum-like models remain useful for studying persistent infection in the postmodulator era.

items.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus.
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen's diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

items.title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection.
items.abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

items.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
items.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

items.title: A phase 2a study with SPL84: A novel RNA-targeted approach to restore CFTR function in people with CF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation.
items.abstract: The 3849+10 kb C→T mutation in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) gene leads to aberrant splicing and the inclusion of a cryptic exon harboring a premature stop codon, resulting in the production of non-functional CFTR protein. SPL84 is an inhaled antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designed to correct CFTR splicing and restore functional CFTR expression in people with CF (pwCF) carrying this mutation. This Phase 2a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multiple ascending dose study evaluated safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory efficacy of inhaled SPL84 in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. Participants received once-weekly inhalations of SPL84 (25 or 50 mg) or placebo for 9 weeks. Exploratory efficacy measures included changes in ppFEV1, ppFEF25-75, and CFQ-R respiratory symptom score. Seventeen participants were included in the analysis, with fifteen completing all treatments. SPL84 was well tolerated with no drug-related serious adverse events. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and consistent with the underlying CF disease. Improvements in lung function, defined as change from baseline in ppFEV1≥5, were observed in up to 70% of the treated participants per cohort, accompanied by improvement of additional efficacy outcomes. Inhaled SPL84 demonstrated a favorable safety profile together with encouraging signals of clinical benefit in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. These findings represent, to our knowledge, the first evidence of potential clinical benefit from a nucleic acid-based therapy targeting RNA in a pulmonary disease, supporting further evaluation of SPL84 as a mutation-specific, RNA-targeted treatment.

items.title: Lactate dehydrogenase A-dependent redox control of selective mRNA translation directs monocyte fate commitment.
items.abstract: Monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is a central process that shapes immune responses across diverse contexts, yet how inflammatory cues engage metabolism to instruct monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Here, using a CRISPR-based metabolic screen combined with monocyte-specific perturbations in bacterial lung infection, we identified lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) as a key metabolic regulator of monocyte commitment to the nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2)+ macrophage fate in vivo. LDHA-dependent cytosolic nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) regeneration enabled selective hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1α) translation through its 5' untranslated region (UTR) and is associated with structural remodeling of this region. HIF1α then functioned as a downstream effector that promoted the NOS2+ macrophage fate. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) further acted as an upstream metabolic priming signal that enhanced LDHA-dependent HIF1α regulation and supported this differentiation process. Together, these findings suggest that metabolic redox state regulates monocyte fate commitment through selective mRNA translation coupled to RNA structural remodeling.

items.title: Development of Versatile Nanoparticle System for Efficient Drug Delivery into Pulmonary Endothelium.
items.abstract: Drug delivery precisely to the pulmonary vasculature represents a formidable challenge. Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (PARDS) is an urgent public health concern accounting for high mortality and long-term morbidity due to severe damage to lung endothelial cells (ECs). Advanced target-specific therapeutic interventions to protect lung vasculature in PARDS are in dire need. FOXF1 protein is a critical mediator of lung angiogenesis and vascular repair after injury. However, whether FOXF1 is a useful pharmacological target for PARDS is unknown. Herein, we developed a universal nanoparticle-based Lung Endothelial Drug Delivery (LEDD) system to deliver hydrophobic small-molecule compounds specifically to lung ECs but not to other cells or organs. Based on single-cell RNA sequencing, FOXF1 expression was decreased in lung ECs in the mouse PARDS model. We used LEDD nanoparticles to restore FOXF1 by delivering a novel FOXF1-activating compound, TanFe[F], which prevents FOXF1 protein degradation. LEDD-TanFe[F] treatment increased FOXF1 protein and its activity in lung ECs in vitro and in vivo. LEDD-TanFe[F] treatment was non-toxic, well-tolerated, and improved mice survival in the PARDS model. LEDD-TanFe[F] reduced endothelial permeability, improved vascular repair, and alveolarization in injured neonatal lungs. LEDD-supported drug delivery precisely to lung ECs is a promising therapeutic approach in PARDS.

items.title: PDHA1 Hyperactivation-Mediated Glucose Metabolism Reprogramming Fuels Neutrophil NETosis and Promotes Acute Lung Injury.
items.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, termed NETosis, is a key driver of lung tissue injury in acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS). However, the precise mechanisms that trigger neutrophil NETosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we observed that neutrophils from both ALI mice and ARDS patients exhibited NETosis alongside a pronounced selective metabolic shift, characterized by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and attenuated glycolytic activity. Phosphoproteomic profiling revealed that this shift was driven by aberrant activation of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 subunit alpha (PDHA1), resulting from its dephosphorylation at Ser293. Inhibiting PDHA1 activity, using either the inhibitor 3-fluoropyruvate (3-FP) or genetic knockdown, effectively reversed this selective metabolic reprogramming and suppressed NETosis. We further constructed neutrophil-targeted 3-FP-loaded albumin nanoparticles (3-FP-BSA NPs). These nanoparticles were specifically taken up by activated neutrophils, markedly inhibited NETosis, and alleviated lipopolysaccharide-induced ALI in mice. Mechanistically, RNA-seq revealed the enrichment of the AMPK in neutrophils during NETosis. AMPK phosphorylated PDHA1 at Ser314, which disrupted the PDHA1-pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 1 (PDK1) interaction and inhibited PDHA1 phosphorylation at Ser293. Ultimately, PDHA1 hyperactivation-driven selective metabolic reprogramming precipitated mitochondrial stress and mtROS accumulation, thereby initiating NETosis. This study defines a targetable metabolic pathway in neutrophils and advances a specific PDHA1-nanotherapeutic strategy against ALI/ARDS.

Nedd4L-mediated stabilization of morphogenetic protein receptor 2 in lung fibroblasts confers protection against pulmonary fibrosis.
items.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an interstitial lung disease that advances over time and is ultimately life-threatening. Despite advances in antifibrotic therapies, disease progression remains largely unavoidable, highlighting the necessity for advancing mechanistic research and identifying new therapeutic options. Bone morphogenetic protein receptor 2 (BMPR2) is a key receptor for BMP signaling and exerts potent antifibrotic role in lung fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms regulating BMPR2 protein stability in fibrotic lungs remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify that the E3 ubiquitin ligase neural precursor cell expressed developmentally downregulated protein 4-like (Nedd4L) as a critical regulator of BMPR2 stability in lung fibroblasts. BMPR2 levels are markedly reduced in lung fibroblasts derived from patients with IPF and in lung tissues from experimental lung fibrosis models. Mechanically, elevated lipid peroxidation in fibrotic lungs induces K48-linked ubiquitination of BMPR2, leading to its degradation and attenuation of BMPs-induced Smad1/5 phosphorylation. Notably, Nedd4L overexpression counteracts lipid peroxidation-induced BMPR2 degradation and promotes BMPs/BMPR2 signaling by shifting BMPR2 ubiquitination toward a stabilizing K63-linked polyubiquitination in lung fibroblasts. We further show that Nedd4L is regulated through threonine phosphorylated by Raf1 kinase in response to increased lipid peroxidation. In vivo, fibroblast-Nedd4L-deficient mice exacerbates experimental lung fibrosis, which is significantly alleviated by BMPR2 overexpression. Collectively, our findings reveal a previously unrecoganized regulatory mechanism of BMPR2 degradation in fibrotic lungs and indicate that stabilizing BMPR2 in lung fibroblasts may represent a promising approach for the treatment of lung fibrosis.

items.title: PUS7-Mediated Pseudouridylation of TGFBI Drives Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening cardiovascular disorder characterized by irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling and poor prognosis. RNA pseudouridylation, the most evolutionarily conserved RNA epigenetic modification, and its catalytic enzyme pseudouridine synthase 7 (PUS7) remained uncharacterized in PH, representing a major gap in the understanding of the epigenetic pathogenesis of the disease. We generated the first single-base resolution pseudouridine (Ψ) landscape in lung tissues of patients with PH using bisulfite-induced deletion sequencing. PUS7 expression was analyzed in hypoxic pulmonary artery endothelial cells, the lung tissues of patients with PH, and SU5416-hypoxia rodent model. The functional roles of PUS7 were investigated through genetic manipulation (PUS7-deficiency cells, adeno-associated virus serotype-mediated overexpression, endothelial cell-specific knockdown, and heterozygous knockout mice) and pharmacological inhibition with NSC107512. Bisulfite-induced deletion sequencing revealed global Ψ dysregulation in the lung tissues of patients with PH. Among PUS family members, PUS7 was the most markedly upregulated in these tissues and in the hypoxic pulmonary artery endothelial cells. Both gene knockdown and pharmacological inhibition with NSC107512 ameliorated PH, whereas adeno-associated virus serotype-mediated PUS7 overexpression exacerbated disease progression. RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing and mutagenesis studies demonstrated that PUS7 bound to and catalyzed Ψ at position 688 of TGFBI (transforming growth factor β-induced protein) mRNA, thereby stabilizing TGFBI and activating phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B signaling pathway. Furthermore, hypoxia-inducible factor 2α bound directly to the PUS7 promoter, establishing a hypoxia-inducible factor 2α/PUS7/TGFBI/phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B positive feedback loop that drives PH pathogenesis. PUS7-mediated pseudouridylation serves as a novel epigenetic driver of PH through the hypoxia-inducible factor 2α/PUS7/TGFBI/phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B axis, positioning PUS7 as a promising therapeutic target for this devastating disease.

items.title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis.
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils.

items.title: Dominant lung involvement and heterozygous IFIH1 variants.
items.abstract: Heterozygous gain-of-function (GoF) variants in IFIH1 are associated with rare autoinflammatory diseases characterized by heightened interferons-stimulated gene (ISG) signatures. These include Aicardi-Goutières syndrome, presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis of the lower limbs, intracerebral calcifications, and neuroinflammation, and Singleton-Merten syndrome, defined by tooth loss, bone demineralization, and vascular calcification. Do rare IFIH1 GoF variants contribute to an interstitial lung disease phenotype, thereby expanding the spectrum of IFIH1-related disorders? Among 559 children with interstitial lung disease (chILD) and exome sequencing as part of their diagnostic work-up, 12 rare heterozygous IFIH1 variants were identified. Of these, 10 were missense variants of unknown significance, which were functionally assessed in vitro using luciferase assay and ISG-expression profiling. Genome-wide RNA analysis was performed on available patient samples to explore broader transcriptional effects. Four variants with increased basal IFNβ transcription in vitro and elevated ISG expression in vivo indicating GoF behaviour were identified. Disease severity correlated with GoF potential of the respective variant. Two patients harbouring IFIH1 variants with strong GoF activity displayed multisystem involvement and died from respiratory failure at 3 and 4 months of age, respectively. Two additional patients showed milder phenotypes with chronic lung disease stabilizing by the age of 8 and 10 years, respectively. Lung biopsies showed alveolar hypoplasia and alveolar macrophage pneumonia (=desquamative interstitial pneumonia) of varying severity. We report a dominant interstitial lung disease phenotype in individuals harbouring novel IFIH1 variants, expanding IFIH1-related disease to the group of type I interferonopathies with pulmonary manifestations like STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI) and COPA syndrome.

items.title: Pulmonary ILC2 Priming as a Link Between Severe Early-Life RSV Bronchiolitis and Asthma.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved. Airway samples from infants with severe RSV disease and experimental models show robust IL-33 responses and pulmonary group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) activation during acute infection. Additionally, neonatal IL-33 and allergen-rechallenge studies demonstrate that ILC2s can persist and acquire memory-like properties. These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. Beyond limited interferon control and prolonged epithelial injury, which may amplify IL-33/ST2 signaling during a developmental window when long-lived lung ILC2 populations are established, we focus on additional candidate mechanisms that could sustain this priming. These include metabolic pathways governing glycolysis, lipid utilization, iron uptake, and mitochondrial function; epigenetic mechanisms involving chromatin remodeling and histone or DNA modifications; and neuroimmune signals that regulate ILC2 activation and recall. Direct evidence that RSV induces durable, cell-intrinsic metabolic, epigenetic, or neuroimmune reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is currently lacking. Longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer of RSV-experienced versus control ILC2s are needed to test this model. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies now provide an opportunity to determine whether preventing severe early-life RSV disease alters airway immune programming and subsequent asthma risk.

items.title: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis in a monogenic mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome.
items.abstract: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare, most often idiopathic fibrotic lung disease with poor prognosis, mainly affecting adults. Biallelic pathogenic variants in the deoxyguanosine kinase gene (DGUOK) cause a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion syndrome, predominantly affecting infants with severe hepatic and neurological disease. Neither detailed pulmonary manifestations nor a pulmonary-dominant phenotype has been reported. We describe nine patients with PPFE and DGUOK-associated mitochondriopathy. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were systematically collected from all patients. Functional studies, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNAseq), immunofluorescence staining, transmission electron microscopy, respiratory chain enzyme activity assays and mtDNA recovery experiment were conducted on patient-derived fibroblasts, muscle or lung tissues. mtDNA content quantification was performed on whole genome sequencing data. All patients (ages 5-36 years) carried biallelic pathogenic DGUOK variants, including an unreported intronic alteration in seven. All presented with progressive dyspnea, weight loss and some with pneumothoraces. Chest computed tomography and lung biopsies demonstrated features of PPFE. snRNAseq of lung tissue from four pediatric patients identified Aberrant Basaloid cells at the fibrotic edge, together with a transcriptional signature of nuclear DNA damage response. Ultrastructural analysis confirmed mitochondrial abnormalities in alveolar type 2 and Aberrant Basaloid cells. This study provides evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction can contribute to early-onset PPFE independent of age, with a DNA damage response signature in aberrant epithelial cell populations previously described only in adult fibrotic lung disease. DGUOK deficiency and other hereditary mitochondrial disorders should be considered in children and young adults presenting with PPFE of unknown origin.

items.title: Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
items.abstract: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave-corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m2, P<0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P<0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P<0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P<0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P<0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P=0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid-A wave PAWP (R2=0.96 versus R2=0.86, P<0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P<0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.86]; P<0.001). More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

items.title: Rare Coding Variants in FOXF1 are Associated with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
items.abstract: Most patients with nonheritable forms of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) lack identifiable pathogenic variants. Increasing evidence suggests that, in addition to high-impact predicted loss-of-function variants, rare missense coding variants may also contribute to disease pathogenesis. We identified ultra-rare missense variants in FOXF1 in two index cases with PAH. FOXF1 encodes a highly conserved transcription factor essential for lung vascular development. We sought to define the frequency of FOXF1 variants, characterize FOXF1 expression, and assess the functional relevance of FOXF1 alterations in PAH. Three independent international PAH cohorts were analyzed for predicted deleterious FOXF1 variants. FOXF1 expression was evaluated using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence. Bioinformatic and chromatin-profiling approaches were used to identify potential downstream transcriptional targets, followed by promoter-reporter assays in vitro. Nine novel and one rare missense variants, one start-site variant, and one in-frame deletion in FOXF1 were identified across the three cohorts. FOXF1 expression was reduced in PAH lungs and localized predominantly to the endothelial cell compartment. Histopathological analysis revealed heterogeneous FOXF1 expression, with the lowest levels in phenotypically abnormal endothelial cells within complex vascular lesions. Single-cell analyses confirmed reduced endothelial FOXF1 expression in PAH, whereas broad FOXF1 downregulation across endothelial populations was not observed in other chronic lung diseases. Integration of CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq identified a canonical FOXF1-binding motif within the BMPR2 promoter. Promoter-reporter assays further supported FOXF1-dependent transcriptional regulation of BMPR2 and demonstrated reduced transcriptional activity of PAH-associated FOXF1 variants. Large-scale genomic and transcriptomic analyses support an association between FOXF1 dysregulation and PAH and identify BMPR2 as a potential downstream transcriptional target.

items.title: Single-cell atlas of fetal immunity across lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood in nonhuman primates.
items.abstract: The fetal immune system develops within a tightly regulated environment that balances immune tolerance with readiness for postnatal antigen exposure. However, limited fetal tissue access constrains understanding of immune ontogeny across compartments. Here we present a multi-tissue single-cell transcriptional atlas of the late-gestation (GD130-135) rhesus macaque fetal immune system, profiling leukocytes from lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood (UCBMC) spanning myeloid, lymphoid, innate lymphoid, and hematopoietic stem cell lineages. Fetal lung is enriched in myeloid cells and ILC2s and shows a proinflammatory bias. Spleen is dominated by T and B cells, with B cells showing enhanced signatures of V(D)J recombination and isotype switching and CD4 T cells showing increased activation and Treg frequency. UCBMC is predominantly composed of T cells with a regulatory transcriptional landscape. Spectral flow cytometry and functional assays corroborate these tissue-specific differences revealing elevated secretion of inflammatory mediators in fetal lung at rest, while spleen and UCBMC show greater inducible responses following stimulation. Together, these data provide a comprehensive cross-tissue atlas of late-gestation primate fetal immunity, revealing tissue-specific immune specialization, functional capacity, and intercellular communication networks that shape immune readiness prior to birth.

items.title: Long-term immunoprophylaxis by TLR9 ligand mediates macrophage-ILC cross-talk against respiratory viral infection.
items.abstract: Rapid development of host immunity is critical during the emergence of viral outbreaks when vaccines are not yet available. Here, we demonstrate that CpG oligodeoxynucleotide-schizophyllan complex (K3-SPG) induces antigen-independent, long-term protection against lethal respiratory virus infection. A single intranasal administration successfully enhanced host resistance to infection for as long as 100 days posttreatment. Mechanistically, we observed a lung-restricted biphasic innate activation of macrophages and innate lymphoid cells. Early protection was mediated by CD11b+CD11c+ macrophages (DP MΦ) and monocyte-derived interstitial macrophages (IMΦ). Late protection was mediated by innate lymphoid cells that were epigenetically reprogrammed, suggesting that two distinct innate immune subsets contribute to the maintenance of disease tolerance in the lung microenvironment. Deficiency of TLR9 or TNF-α abrogated innate activation and protective immunity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that adjuvant-induced prophylaxis is a promising approach to enhancing host resistance against respiratory virus infection, involving the biphasic cooperation between innate immune cells in the local tissue.

items.title: Influenza A virus infection induces immune dysregulation in the placenta and fetus without vertical transmission in nonhuman primates.
items.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection during pregnancy is associated with stillbirth and preterm birth. We hypothesized that maternal IAV infection disrupts placental and fetal immune networks in ways that correlate with disease severity. Pregnant pigtail macaques were inoculated with IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)] and underwent delivery and fetal necropsy 5 days postinfection (N = 11), with comparison to uninfected controls (N = 16). Stillbirth occurred in 18% of infected pregnancies and in no controls. Although vertical transmission was not observed, low levels of viral RNA were detected in two placentas. Maternal infection was associated with induction of a type I interferon response in the placenta and altered innate and adaptive immune cell populations in the fetus. Maternal disease metrics (e.g., lung viral load and interferon-α) were rarely associated with placental immune perturbations but frequently linked to fetal immune cell populations (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and monocyte subsets). Collectively, these data indicate that maternal IAV disease severity is associated with dysregulated fetal immunity.

items.title: Mitigating lateral sensing blind spots: A dual-segment bronchoscopic robot with a bioinspired skin.
items.abstract: Lateral force blind spots frequently trigger airway injuries during robotic bronchoscopy. Traditional sensing approaches lack fine spatial resolution, and single-segment robots suffer poor posture adjustment flexibility, worsening unmonitored tissue contact. We integrate a snake-scale-inspired 64-channel gradient piezoelectric film with a dual-segment manipulator to resolve lateral blind spots for secure bronchial navigation. The conformally wrapped sensor delivers fast (<10 ms), precise force detection (R2 > 0.98, RMSE < 0.145 N, CV < 2%) and filters bending pseudo-forces. The dual-segment design enables coordinated proximal-distal motion to avoid overcontact in tortuous lumens. Phantom and ex vivo porcine lung tests confirm real-time force localization, 5.0 N safety alarms, and autonomous tuning to keep contact forces below 3.0 N. This synergistic robot-sensor design supplies a translatable safety control strategy for flexible surgical manipulators.

items.title: Mechanosensitive Stanniocalcin-1 Suppresses Smooth Muscle Cell Proliferation and Attenuates Experimental Pulmonary Hypertension.
items.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) is driven by progressive vascular remodeling, particularly smooth muscle cell (SMC) proliferation. Current combination vasodilator therapies have markedly improved outcomes; however, prognosis remains poor in subgroups such as patients with respiratory comorbidities. Elevation of intravascular hydrostatic pressure is a hallmark of IPAH, yet its direct role in pulmonary artery SMCs remains unclear. We aimed to identify pressure-responsive mediators using a newly developed hydrostatic pressurization system to model hypertensive hemodynamics. Pulmonary artery SMCs from 4 patients with IPAH were exposed to high hydrostatic pressure (70/40 mm Hg, 60 bpm). Transcriptomic profiling identified differentially expressed genes, which were validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Functional studies included PIEZO1 (piezo type mechanosensitive ion channel component 1) modulation, rhSTC1 (recombinant human stanniocalcin-1) treatment, bromodeoxyuridine incorporation, and Western blotting for cell-cycle regulators. Chronic hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension was assessed in wild-type and Stc1-/- mice by hemodynamic and histological analyses, with or without intratracheal rhSTC1 administration. RNA sequencing revealed STC1 to be a pressure-induced gene in IPAH SMCs. PIEZO1 activation upregulated STC1, whereas knockdown blunted this response. STC1 was upregulated in IPAH lungs, while rhSTC1 reduced pulmonary arterial SMC proliferation and increased p-p53, p21, and p27 expression. Stc1-/- mice under hypoxia exhibited significantly higher right ventricular systolic pressure and greater pulmonary arterial medial thickness than wild-type mice. CD68-positive macrophages were increased in Stc1-/- mice under normoxia and further elevated with hypoxia. Intratracheal administration of rhSTC1 attenuated PAH in wild-type and Stc1-/- mice. Elevated hydrostatic pressure drives STC1 expression via PIEZO1, suggesting an adaptive but insufficient protective response in IPAH. Modulation of STC1 (stanniocalcin-1) may represent a potential therapeutic approach.

items.title: A transcriptomic atlas of chronic lung allograft dysfunction.
items.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is the leading cause of late mortality after lung transplantation. Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) and restrictive allograft syndrome (RAS) are the main underlying clinical entities. Their molecular and cellular signatures are unclear and, therefore, we aimed to identify molecular programmes associated with morphological disease severity in CLAD. We performed high-resolution imaging-based gene expression profiling of 128 lung samples from explanted CLAD and donor lungs, using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, cellular and pathway enrichment, and hub gene identification. Findings were validated across four datasets, including a murine transplant model, human BOS lungs, transbronchial biopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of lung transplant recipients. Unsupervised clustering revealed two transcriptomic CLAD endotypes aligning with mild-fibrotic (BOS, mild RAS) and advanced-fibrotic disease (moderate/severe RAS). Samples from the same patient often diverged molecularly, underscoring intrapatient heterogeneity and limitations of current phenotypical classification. Five molecular programmes emerged: 1) epithelial stress and innate immunity in early-fibrotic CLAD; 2) progressive adaptive immunity and cytotoxicity in advanced CLAD; 3) transient extracellular matrix remodelling; 4) progressive endothelial loss/dysfunction; and 5) progressive loss of homeostasis, wherein multiple potential druggable targets were detected. Finally, we identified a 26 CLAD-hub-gene panel, which showed robust diagnostic performance to discriminate CLAD. CLAD is a spatially heterogeneous, yet molecularly continuous disease process, wherein BOS and RAS represent variable stages of a shared immunopathological continuum. Our findings support the development of lung-specific molecular classifiers to guide diagnostics and reveal novel targets for personalised therapies in transplantation.

items.title: Nasal nitric oxide combined with clinical features for preliminary screening of primary ciliary dyskinesia in bronchiectasis.
items.abstract: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), an underdiagnosed genetic disorder characterised by dysfunctional cilia, is a known cause of bronchiectasis. To prospectively identify PCD among patients with bronchiectasis using nasal nitric oxide (nNO) and clinical features, and to characterise genetic features. This cross-sectional study enrolled adolescent and adult patients with bronchiectasis from the BE-China registry at Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital. Individuals with either strong clinical suspicion or nNO ≤77 nL·min-1 received a structured diagnostic work-up, including transmission electron microscopy and whole-exome sequencing. Diagnoses followed the 2025 European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society PCD diagnostic guidelines. Among 373 patients with bronchiectasis, 27 (7.4%) were in the PCD group (14 "confirmed PCD" and 13 "PCD highly likely"). nNO showed high screening accuracy (sensitivity 84.8%, specificity 97.1%). Patients with PCD were younger and had earlier bronchiectasis onset. Age-adjusted regression analysis showed independent associations between PCD and lower body mass index (regression coefficient (RC) -1.5, 95% CI -2.9 to -0.1), forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) % predicted (RC -18.4, 95% CI -28.3 to -8.6), forced vital capacity (FVC) % predicted (RC -11.3, 95% CI -19.5 to -3.0), and FEV1/FVC (RC -10.3, 95% CI -16.9 to -3.8). Strong associations were observed with rhinosinusitis (OR 25.3, 95% CI 8.8 to 92.1) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection (OR 8.5, 95% CI 3.2 to 25.7). Situs inversus occurred in 25.9% of patients with PCD. DNAH11 was the most common pathogenic gene. Patients with PCD had more severe disease, reinforcing the need for structured screening in patients with bronchiectasis. nNO combined with clinical features is an effective and reliable screening strategy for PCD in bronchiectasis.

items.title: Alkylating Agent-Induced FANCL Impairment Damages Pulmonary Arterial, Venous, and Microvascular Endothelial Cells and Predisposes to PAH/PVOD.
items.abstract: Alkylating chemotherapies such as mitomycin C (MMC) and cisplatin (CDDP) are associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) features, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using established MMC and newly developed CDDP rat models, we found that both agents induced PAH/PVOD, as evidenced by elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, pulmonary arterial, venous and microvascular remodeling, and right ventricular dysfunction, with MMC causing more severe pathology. In cultured pulmonary arterial, venous, and microvascular endothelial cells, MMC and CDDP induced elevated DNA damage, apoptosis, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, together with impaired angiogenic capacity, proliferation, and barrier junction. These phenotypical changes were accompanied by conserved Fanconi anemia complementation group L (FANCL) downregulation. FANCL deficiency in mice drove spontaneous and exacerbated CDDP‑induced PAH/PVOD, whereas AAV‑mediated FANCL rescue or treatment with a DNA protector, amifostine, significantly attenuated the disease pathogenesis in mouse and rat models. Collectively, this study establishes a novel CDDP‑induced rat model, identifies a conserved FANCL-DNA damage-endothelial dysfunction mechanistic axis underlying PAH/PVOD induced by MMC or CDDP, and highlights FANCL rescue and DNA damage inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies for this severe form of pulmonary vascular disease.

items.title: Transplantation of endothelial progenitor cells attenuates pulmonary fibrosis via IFITM3-containing exosomes.
items.abstract: Endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) are critical for vascular regeneration after injury. However, their role in pulmonary fibrosis (PF) remains unclear. Here, we identified a previously unrecognized population of lung capillary EPCs coexpressing c-KIT and FOXF1 (capEPCs) in adult human and mouse lungs. capEPCs were significantly reduced in lungs from patients with PF and in bleomycin-injured mice, implicating loss of this regenerative endothelial population in disease pathogenesis. Transplantation of donor capEPCs attenuated experimental PF, improved survival, reduced collagen deposition, and restored lung function. Donor capEPCs engrafted into the lung microcirculation of bleomycin-injured mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 as a highly enriched transcript in capEPCs. Conditioned media from IFITM3-overexpressing EPCs or recombinant IFITM3 enhanced endothelial proliferation and angiogenesis while suppressing TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation in vitro. IFITM3 was found in capEPC-derived exosomes. Treatment with IFITM3-containing exosomes recapitulated the therapeutic effects of capEPC transplantation by improving endothelial function, inhibiting fibroblast activation, increasing animal survival, reducing lung fibrosis, and restoring lung function. Together these findings identified capEPC deficiency as a feature of PF and demonstrated that IFITM3-containing exosomes promoted vascular repair. Restoration of capEPC regenerative function or delivery of IFITM3-enriched exosomes may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for human PF.

items.title: Modeling Respiratory Infections Using Patient-Derived Apical-Out Airway Organoids.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Airway organoids bridge the gap between conventional epithelial cultures and animal models by combining human tissue architecture, cellular diversity, and experimental accessibility. However, because these systems are dynamic, reproducible infection modeling requires careful definition of parameters influencing infection readouts, including epithelial polarity, maturation, cellular composition, and access to a physiologically relevant apical surface. We established patient-derived apical-out airway organoids and characterized them longitudinally using multiple modalities throughout differentiation, followed by proof-of-concept viral infection and host-response profiling. Organoids generated from resected human lung tissue were converted from an apical-in to an apical-out orientation and maintained in suspension. Over 21 days, they retained outward-facing apical features and matured from basal-cell-enriched structures into airway-like epithelium containing goblet cells, microvilli, ionocytes and ciliated cells, with mucus production and motile surface cilia. This time-resolved characterization demonstrated changes in organoid growth, epithelial organization, and lineage composition, guiding selection of maturation stages for infection experiments. Exposure of the apical surface to GFP-expressing human metapneumovirus (hMPV) enabled infection without disruptive shearing or microinjection. Viral fluorescence and immunostaining confirmed hMPV infection and revealed associated cytopathic changes in infected organoids. Infection efficiency and cellular tropism varied across maturation stages. Bulk RNA sequencing of infected versus mock-infected organoids showed reproducibly distinct transcriptional profiles and enrichment of antiviral and innate immune pathways. These findings demonstrate that the epithelial features shaping infection readouts must be defined empirically within each organoid system through longitudinal, multimodal characterization, thereby supporting rigorous interpretation and reproducible application in mechanistic and translational respiratory infection studies.

items.title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses.
items.abstract: Tissue-resident immunity constitutes a first line of defence against pathogens and enables rapid innate and adaptive memory responses1-3. However, experimental studies have been hindered by a lack of holistic human in vitro models that enable epithelial infection in the context of tissue-resident immune subsets. In lung, differing notions of transient versus sustained residency of tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM cells) have challenged the extent to which anamnestic recall immunity to respiratory pathogens occurs locally or in concert with secondary lymphoid organs4-6. Here we generated long-term adult human distal lung organoids from intact tissue fragments in 3D air-liquid interface culture, which co-preserved epithelial and stromal components with endogenous lung-resident immune cells (T cells, B cells, natural killer cells and myeloid cells). The organoid T cells expressed residency and memory markers and preserved T cell receptor repertoires of cognate fresh tissue. SARS-CoV-2 infected the organoid lung epithelium, stimulated inflammatory cytokine production and, crucially, induced SARS-CoV-2-specific, tissue-resident T cell responses. Furthermore, boosting T cells within intact organoids with SARS-CoV-2 peptide pools blunted subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with a component of virus-specific protective TRM cell function in the absence of secondary lymphoid tissues. Overall, this immunocompetent lung organoid system demonstrates functional control of viral infection by lung-intrinsic memory T cell responses, provides a rationale for local vaccination strategies and validates a general platform for investigation of human tissue-resident immunity in health and disease.

items.title: Nerandomilast's Antifibrotic Effects Are Modulated by the tRF-AKAP12-PKA Axis in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
items.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) involves persistent fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, and tissue stiffening. The role of oxidatively modified tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) in linking fibroblast activation to mechanotransduction remains unclear. 5o8G tRF-1-AspGTC (tRF) expression was analyzed in lung tissues from patients with PF and experimental mouse models. Gain- and loss-of-function approaches were used to define its role in fibroblast activation and PF progression. Mechanistic studies examined the tRF-AKAP12-PKA-YAP pathway, and therapeutic relevance was evaluated by assessing the antifibrotic efficacy of Nerandomilast under AKAP12-deficient or AKAP12-restored conditions. tRF was markedly upregulated in fibrotic lung tissues from PF patients and experimental mice. Myofibroblast-specific inhibition of this tRF significantly attenuated PF in mice. Consistently, tRF accumulation promoted fibroblast activation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and profibrotic phenotypes in human pulmonary fibroblasts (HPFs). Mechanistically, tRF directly targeted and suppressed AKAP12 expression, thereby disrupting the AKAP12-PKA signaling complex. Loss of AKAP12 disrupted AKAP12-dependent PKA compartmentalization, altered PKA substrate phosphorylation, and promoted cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP-dependent mechanotransduction. Importantly, AKAP12 deficiency impaired Nerandomilast-mediated restoration of PKA-YAP signaling and limited its antifibrotic efficacy, whereas AKAP12 restoration re-established this signaling axis and synergistically enhanced Nerandomilast therapeutic effects in PF mice. tRF promotes PF by disrupting AKAP12-dependent spatial PKA signaling and activating YAP-dependent mechanotransduction. Targeting the tRF-AKAP12 axis, particularly through AKAP12 restoration, may improve Nerandomilast-based therapy.

items.title: Mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction in airway epithelial cells promotes goblet cell metaplasia and more severe asthma.
items.abstract: Type 2 (T2) inflammation is a defining feature of asthma and associated with epithelial dysfunction, including goblet cell metaplasia and ciliary loss. Here, we investigated whether T2 inflammation and associated 15 lipoxygenase-1 (15LO1) activity alters mitochondrial metabolism in airway epithelial cells (AECs) and contributes to disease pathophysiology. Freshly isolated AECs from T2-high asthmatic participants exhibited increased oxygen consumption rates (OCR), including elevated basal respiration and proton leak, alongside reduced coupling efficiency compared to T2-low participants. These functional changes were accompanied by increased expression of electron transport chain (ETC) proteins, worse lung function and epithelial phenotypic changes. In vitro, IL-13 stimulation of differentiated AECs recapitulated these findings, inducing higher OCR, increased ETC protein levels, and enhanced proton leak while paradoxically reducing intracellular ATP. These metabolic alterations are associated with increased uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) expression and goblet cell differentiation. Mechanistically, 15LO1 emerged as a key regulator, as ALOX15 knockdown or pharmacologic inhibition reduced OCR parameters, ETC protein expression, UCP2, and goblet cell markers, without effect on ATP levels, suggesting additional regulatory mechanisms. Collectively, these findings identify a metabolic axis linking T2 inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and airway epithelial metabolism, while highlighting 15LO1-driven mitochondrial uncoupling as a potential therapeutic target in asthma. .

items.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal key immunological and metabolic correlates of mortality in HIV-associated Pneumocystis pneumonia.
items.abstract: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) remains a major cause of life-threatening respiratory failure in people with advanced HIV, yet the biological factors associated with mortality are incompletely understood. We performed integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from 42 adults with HIV-associated PCP, relating molecular signatures to mortality. We found that fungal burden, measured by sputum immunofluorescence, Pneumocystis qPCR, and 1,3-β-D-glucan, did not differ between survivors and non-survivors or correlate with baseline gas exchange. Instead, non-survivors exhibited a bronchoalveolar immunometabolic failure signature characterised by marked depletion of immunoglobulins and complement, reduced pattern recognition receptors and fibroblast growth factor family proteins, and broad disruption of extracellular matrix organisation. Metabolomic profiling revealed enrichment of arginine-urea cycle and tricarboxylic acid pathways, with coordinated accumulation of arginine, citrulline, and TCA cycle intermediates consistent with nitrosative and mitochondrial stress.
